This supports the Central-Peripheral Dichotomy theory, which proposes fundamentally distinct computational specializations --- visual recognition and attentional selection, respectively --- in the central and peripheral visual fields.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We introduce a mean-reverting stochastic differential equation with a three-component stochastic term and show that it generates a hierarchy of steady-state (stationary) distributions. At the top level, the hierarchy is described by a modified-Beta distribution, while one- and two-parameter reductions produce compact-support, power-law-tailed, and exponential-type limiting families within a single stochastic framework. We then construct two generalized extensions of this hierarchy. In the first, the power transformation is applied directly at the level of the stochastic differential equation; in the second, the same transformation is applied only after the stationary modified-Beta hierarchy has been obtained. While these two procedures agree on important lower branches and limiting cases they generally differ at the top level. The generalized hierarchy is therefore not unique: nonlinear transformation and stationary-state reduction do not commute. For both routes, we derive the probability density and cumulative distribution functions, express their parameters in terms of the underlying stochastic dynamics, clarify the relations among their limiting cases, and compare the resulting families with the traditional Generalized Beta framework.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Small tabular datasets with expert-designed spectral features are the norm in operational Earth observation, and the networks applied to them are typically hand-designed. We revisit one such published model -- a Sentinel-2 algal bloom classifier -- and ask what architecture search adds, holding the task, the features and the lake-level train/test split of the original study fixed. Searching an extended multilayer-perceptron space with regularized evolution, and selecting on inner-cross-validation AUC only, we find networks that improve held-out AUC from 0.790 to 0.820 and accuracy from 0.733 to 0.748 while using 409 trainable parameters, 26 times fewer than the strongest hand-designed reference. The search converges on a consistent recipe -- a single narrow layer, RMS normalisation, $\tanh$ activation, step-decayed RMSprop and weight averaging -- that a practitioner would be unlikely to reach by default. At 1.6\,kB the resulting model is small enough to serve as an onboard screening trigger, which is the setting that motivates the work. Code: https://github.com/VU-AIML/automl4eo-bloom-nas.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Despite decades of data quality (DQ) research, a gap remains between DQ dimensions, such as accuracy or completeness, which the literature defines in textual form, and DQ tools, which typically implement low-level checks that are not aligned with these dimensions. ISO/IEC 25024 and ISO/IEC 5259 attempt to bridge this gap by defining DQ metrics for each dimension. However, these DQ metrics are hardly used, because the standards leave open how to implement them: for example, the metric for syntactic accuracy counts syntactically accurate values, but does not state how to decide that a value is syntactically accurate. This simply moves the problem to another level without solving it. As a result, DQ assessment currently cannot build on the standards. In this paper, we make the ISO DQ metrics executable. We classify all data-level metrics of both standards into (i) generalizable metrics that need no input beyond the data, (ii) parameterized metrics whose parameters can be learned from clean reference data or set by an expert, and (iii) non-generalizable metrics that need qualitative judgment and cannot be automated. For the metrics that can be automated, i.e., categories (i) and (ii), we propose implementation guidelines that resolve what the standards leave open. We realize the guidelines in dqmeasure, an open-source library of 20 metrics that learns these parameters from reference data instead of relying on manually defined rules. Our experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets show that the metric scores decrease monotonically with an increasing number of injected errors, decline together with downstream ML performance, and scale linearly with the number of rows, which enables automated DQ monitoring based on the standards.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Appearance-based gaze estimation offers a low-cost alternative to infrared eye tracking for screen-based behavioral and clinical applications, however existing models are typically developed for wide ranges of gaze angle and head pose. Prolonged screen viewing presents a distinct regime in which gaze remains near the screen center, head motion is limited, and calibration drift accumulates over time. In this work, we benchmark six published estimators along with a proposed differential-gaze model on 140 long-duration facial video recordings with synchronized eye tracking under subject-disjoint evaluation and a common budget of calibration frames. Differential estimation was the only static method that significantly improved upon a baseline predictor of each recording's mean gaze, and was further boosted by addition of temporal context. It also yielded the strongest agreement with reference fixations and saccades, demonstrating that low angular error alone could not validate eye movement reconstruction. These findings establish differential estimation as a promising foundation for reliable gaze tracking in long-duration, narrow-range settings.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Theories of how the brain processes information and returns intelligent outputs are numerous and often difficult to conclusively test. Here, we consider an approach grounded in informatics and algorithmic thermodynamics for how neural systems respond to different patterns of information in different ways, with a focus on the relationship between the information entropy of a signal and a new proposed quantity we term information enthalpy, which represents the internal resource of structured information within a system available to be used for predictions and other forms of work. To evaluate the capacity of the external signals to increase information enthalpy in the system, we introduce the information enthalpy potential (IEP) as a defined metric. We propose and implement a method for quantifying the amount of potential information enthalpy - the IEP - in a given signal across a range of example signals. We offer a conjecture of how information enthalpy may be treated by neural systems within a biological framework before showing how it may integrate and offer falsifiability to existing approaches such as the Free Energy Principle. This framework is also positioned in light of the role of neural criticality. Finally, we postulate a testable and falsifiable framework where the distinct mechanisms within each driver interact through a described n-body-inspired model to govern the "motion" of a neural system through a high dimensional state-space. Through these processes, it is proposed that these features form the most fundamental basis of the neural drivers that give rise to the complexity of adaptive behaviors that are commonly called: intelligence.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Cross-modal vector retrieval is widely used in multimodal systems, such as search engines and vector databases. It typically operates in out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, where query vectors follow a distribution that differs from that of the vectors stored in the database. In such cases, conventional indexes suffer significant performance degradation, and even methods specially designed for OOD remain limited by inefficient use of query modal characteristics, restricted GPU parallelism, and inadequate support for dynamic updates. We present CORAL, a novel GPU-accelerated graph-based vector index for scalable cross-modal retrieval, featuring hierarchical memory management that spans GPU, CPU, and disk. Specifically, CORAL incrementally incorporates the characteristics of query modality and terminates index construction timely. Crucially, it introduces coverage-aware adaptive pruning to address the imbalanced coverage of the query vector's neighbors. Moreover, CORAL presents a fully neighborhood-aware projection approach to efficiently utilize GPUs for highly parallel index construction, and a targeted connectivity enhancement method to refine the index structure. Besides, CORAL also supports modal-semantics-based vector insertion and topology-repairing deletion that restore node connectivity. Experimental results demonstrate that CORAL outperforms existing methods with up to 1.6 times the throughput at matched recall while reducing construction time by up to 56%. Furthermore, it exhibits remarkable resilience under dynamic updates and remains effective at the billion scale.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Database systems are predominantly developed in unsafe languages (e.g., C/C++) to meet performance requirements through low-level memory management, yet this reliance renders them prone to systemic memory-safety issues that compromise reliability, consistency, security, and durability. Through an extensive bug analysis of prominent database systems, we show that these memory-safety issues persist in production environments despite advancements in database testing tools. While emerging hardware-assisted extensions, such as Arm's Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) and CHERI, offer a promising mitigation path for memory safety, their practical applicability and performance overhead within the specialized constraints of database systems remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we evaluate hardware extensions through the lens of what we define as the database trilemma: the fundamental trade-off between safety, performance, and portability, to determine their viability for production-grade database systems. We provide the first side-by-side comparison of MTE and CHERI across a database workload suite. Our bottom-up study spans microarchitecture, the compiler/runtime/OS stack, core data structures (ART, B+Tree, hash table, skip list, linked list, and queue), and full database systems (Redis, LevelDB, SQLite, MySQL, DuckDB, and LadyBugDB) to characterize their performance, safety guarantees, and ease of adoption. We find that while hardware extensions can offer near-deterministic protection, they introduce non-uniform performance taxes: MTE provides high portability with modest overheads (~10%), while CHERI delivers superior safety guarantees with higher performance penalties (20-60%) and significant porting effort. Our study equips database systems architects with an actionable guide toward building the next generation of reliable, secure databases using hardware-assisted safety mechanisms.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Solving high-dimensional structural model updating problems requires an algorithm capable of navigating complex, non-convex landscapes with correlated parameters. Existing hybrid evolutionary algorithms typically rely on static architectures or fixed switching rules, resulting in disjointed search phases. To address this, this study proposes a Deep Reinforcement Learning-governed dynamic DE-CMAES Orchestration (DRL-DCO) algorithm, in which a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)-based actor-critic agent continuously governs the evolutionary process as a single, unified system rather than a mechanical concatenation of algorithms. Guided by a progression-aware state representation and a diversity-informed reward, the agent fluidly reallocates computational resources between the differencevector-based exploration of Differential Evolution (DE) and the covariance-guided exploitation of CMA-ES, while jointly regulating population size, elite preservation, and a restart mechanism to escape local optima. This allows DRL-DCO to autonomously transition between exploration-dominant, exploitation-dominant, and mixed-strategy regimes across generations. Beyond the training phase, the trained actor can operate in a supervision-free inference mode, where the internalized policy autonomously orchestrates DE and CMA-ES control from observed search states through forward inference alone, without critic evaluation or weight updates, enabling faster deployment while retaining full effectiveness. Validated on high-dimensional single-objective optimization benchmarks and the IASC-ASCE structural health monitoring benchmark, DRL-DCO achieves superior convergence accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art adaptive and hybrid evolutionary algorithms, as well as single-operator DRL-governed baselines.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Recently, academia and industry have considered the problem of approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) with filters. In this setting, each object consists of a high-dimensional vector and attribute values. Given a query vector, filters for attribute values, and $k$, this problem retrieves $k$ vectors approximately nearest to the query vector among a set of objects passing the filters. This paper considers range filters, i.e., users can specify a range constraint for each attribute. Most existing works do not consider this setting, and they assume (i) only a single attribute or (ii) matching filters that require the same attribute values or categories. Existing techniques for these assumptions are not available for our setting or are trivially not efficient. Although standard solutions, such as pre-filter and post-filter, can handle our problem, they are also inefficient. Some works tackle the same problem as ours, but their techniques necessitate historical query workloads, which significantly limit practical use cases. To remove these limitations, this work proposes Grant, a novel framework that solves this problem efficiently while accepting arbitrary range filters and ANNS data structures. Grant can guarantee a search time sub-linear to the number of objects, which is not held by existing techniques. We conduct extensive experiments, and their results demonstrate that Grant outperforms existing techniques.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The centralization of web information raises legal and ethical concerns, particularly in social, healthcare, and education applications. Decentralized architectures offer a promising alternative by keeping data closer to its source, yet efficient query processing remains a significant challenge. Link Traversal Query Processing (LTQP) enables querying across decentralized networks but often suffers from long execution times and high data transfer costs due to the large number of HTTP requests involved. Many queries are highly selective with respect to the data model objects distributed across the network. For example, in a social media application where users store heterogeneous data, a query may target only users' posts and comments, ignoring their other information. We refer to such queries as data-model selective. We propose a shape-based pruning approach that relies on shape indexes and a query-shape subsumption algorithm to reduce the search space and thus the number of HTTP requests. We formalize this approach as a link pruning mechanism for LTQP and evaluate it on social media queries from the SolidBench benchmark across multiple metrics. Our results show that shape-based pruning substantially improves query execution time, first-result arrival time, diefficiency, and network usage for data-model selective queries, while having a negligible impact on non-selective data-model queries. These gains cost only a minor increase in triples per shape-index instance. Our approach is also resilient, retaining its benefits even when some data providers do not supply shape indexes. This work demonstrates that shape-based metadata can significantly optimize LTQP in decentralized knowledge graphs for an important class of queries. By exposing such metadata, data providers not only enhance data quality and interoperability but also improve the efficiency of traversal-based query processing.

The paper develops a theory for selecting the rolling window when generating out-of-sample forecasts with factor-augmented regression (FAR) models in the presence of structural instabilities. It shows how to select a rolling window by minimizing the conditional mean squared forecast error (MSFE) while accounting for uncertainty in factor estimation. Because the conditional MSFE is unobserved and the factors are latent, this paper proposes a feasible version of the criterion and derives conditions under which the new method is asymptotically loss-efficient. A simulation experiment documents the procedure's performance.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The Information Matrix (IM) test is a natural specification check for likelihood-based models, yet cross-sectional implementations are often badly sized, confound neglected heterogeneity with distributional misspecification, and require third derivatives. We develop the panel information matrix (PIM) test for models with fixed effects. Explicit fixed effects isolate functional-form misspecification from time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity. Although the profile maximum likelihood estimator inherits incidental-parameter bias of order $O(1/T)$, the leading bias of the profile PIM is of order $\sqrt{n}/T$, so it is asymptotically negligible whenever $n/T^2\to 0$, which includes the rectangular regime $n/T\to\mathrm{const}$, and stabilizes under parabolic asymptotics $n/T^2\toρ\in(0,\infty)$. This robustness arises because the indicator fluctuates at rate $\sqrt{n}$ rather than $\sqrt{nT}$. The same rate argument makes third-derivative corrections asymptotically unnecessary, so the test uses only first- and second-order likelihood derivatives. Simulations confirm that asymptotic PIM critical values suffice in moderately long panels, even when Wald tests for $θ$ are badly sized, while a parametric bootstrap largely removes size distortions when $ρ>0$.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Program evaluations routinely find larger effects of investment in low-skill children, while structural models of skill formation typically find that skill and investment are complements. I reconcile these findings by introducing the Average Marginal Return (AMR), which averages the marginal return to an input over the distribution of other inputs, providing a structural analogue to the average treatment effects estimated in program evaluations. The AMR reveals why input scales and distributions matter for the economic interpretation of structural estimates, why reduced-form interaction coefficients need not identify technological complementarity, and why dynamic complementarity can be difficult to detect in reduced-form work. I estimate AMRs to parental investment using a dynamic factor model of cognitive and noncognitive skill formation for ages 5-14 in the Children of the NLSY79. I accommodate binary and Likert measures using ordered probits, showing that treating them as continuous substantially biases estimates, and introduce effective factors to extend the scale-invariant normalization of Freyberger (2026) to models with multiple skills per period. Investment in early childhood generates larger long-run gains in cognitive skill than investment at later ages. Although skill and investment are complements, the AMR to early investment is initially flat across skill levels but becomes sharply decreasing in initial skill over time. By ages 13-14, children at the 10th percentile of early cognitive skill gain roughly twice as much from early investment as children at the 90th.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
A challenge in nonlinear filtering is to incorporate nonlinear effects into approximations of the conditional mean while retaining a finite-dimensional recursive algorithm. We derive a second-order asymptotic expansion of the filtering mean with respect to the system-noise intensity. We apply this expansion to the Lorenz--63 model, a prototypical three-dimensional chaotic dynamical system. The first-order approximation is computed using a Kalman--Bucy filter for the system linearized around the deterministic reference trajectory. The second-order correction incorporates the Hessian of the Lorenz--63 drift and is computed through a closed recursive system with 3+9+18=30 independent scalar components. The full system, including the reference trajectory and the first-order mean and covariance, has 42 independent scalar components. To support stable tracking of chaotic trajectories over long time intervals, we introduce recentering of the expansion and redistribution of Gaussian components between expansion orders. In the numerical experiments, we compare the proposed algorithm with an ensemble transform Kalman filter (ETKF) as a practical benchmark and a particle filter (PF) as a numerical reference. Under the full-observation settings, the proposed algorithm achieves a lower root-mean-square error relative to the truth and a smaller distance to the 10,000-particle PF reference than the 20-member ETKF. These results suggest that the proposed second-order extension of Kalman filtering has the potential to balance filtering accuracy and computational cost.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Many neck disorders, from chronic neck pain and headache to thyroid and nodal malignancy and radiation-induced fibrosis, both arise from and alter the mechanical properties of neck tissues, yet clinical assessment still relies on morphology, palpation and symptoms. Ultrasound and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) now allow these properties to be measured in vivo, but the neck literature differs widely in methodology and remains dispersed across modalities and tissues. This review brings together the biomechanical basis of neck tissue behavior, the clinical conditions that alter it, and the principles and applications of ultrasound elastography and MRE in the neck. We show that ultrasound elastography has demonstrated diagnostic value for thyroid nodules and cervical lymph nodes, while neck MRE has been shown to be feasible but remains at an early stage. Across both modalities, reported values depend strongly on fiber orientation, posture, muscle activation and acquisition conditions. We therefore propose reporting recommendations and discuss how measurements beyond stiffness, including anisotropy, viscosity and nonlinearity, could improve disease management and inform computational models of the neck.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We develop standard errors for estimates of causal effects in settings where the distribution of treatment exposures is known but potentially exhibits complicated dependence patterns across units. Such dependence arises, for example, in settings with spillovers/interference across units or when the treatment assignment is spatially correlated. Our variance estimator generalizes several properties of the Neyman variance estimator for completely randomized experiments to general designs: it is unbiased for an upper bound on the variance from the design-based perspective; the conservativeness of this upper bound depends on the heterogeneity of treatment effects; and it is also valid under certain forms of super-population sampling of the potential outcomes. Our estimator reduces to standard approaches in simple designs, such as the Neyman variance estimator in completely randomized experiments and the cluster-robust variance estimator in cluster-randomized experiments. We show that the proposed estimator is admissible among the class of quadratic-form variance estimators, and derive asymptotic conditions under which it is consistent for an upper bound on the asymptotic variance of the treatment effect estimator. In simulations and applications based on two empirical studies, one with peer effects and another with a spatially correlated treatment, we find that the proposed variance estimator performs well, and in some cases yields standard errors that are 2-3 times shorter than those of existing alternatives.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Scalable logic-based analytics are frequently dominated by cyclic multi-way joins over large relational datasets. State-of-the-art systems evaluate these joins through chains of binary joins, incurring substantial overhead from large intermediate relations that must be materialized and redistributed across the network. Worst-Case Optimal Joins (WCOJ) offer a provably superior alternative by evaluating joins one variable at a time, eliminating intermediate blowup. However, existing WCOJ implementations target either shared-memory machines or one-shot, non-recursive queries on dataflow and big-data platforms, leaving WCOJ-based recursive evaluation on distributed-memory HPC systems an open problem. We present, to our knowledge, the first distributed-memory Datalog engine that uses WCOJ for recursive fixpoint evaluation. Our design builds on HyperCube partitioning, which hash-partitions relations along variable-aligned grid dimensions and replicates them along missing dimensions, and extends it from a single shuffle to iterative execution: in every semi-naive iteration, only newly derived tuples are repartitioned and re-replicated, using MPI all-to-all collectives and per-dimension all-gathers over subcube communicators, while the same layout is reused across iterations so that all WCOJ intersections remain rank-local. We evaluate our system on the Aurora and Polaris leadership-class supercomputers at Argonne National Laboratory using graph mining and program analysis benchmarks, demonstrating strong scalability, outperforming state-of-the-art Datalog engines on most benchmarks, and characterizing how partition dimensionality trades runtime against memory feasibility.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Semantic query engines evaluate natural-language filters with a large language model, and every evaluation is a costly oracle call. Optimizers that reduce these calls face a dilemma: cascades that trust a cheap proxy miss their precision and recall targets on many queries, methods with finite-sample guarantees save little, and all of them discard the oracle's labels when the query ends. We present SemViews, a certified semantic filter that orders tuples by signals that cost no oracle calls (the labels that earlier queries left behind as semantic views, a local embedding, and a helper model's score), refines that order with labels it must pay for anyway, and certifies its answer with fresh stratified oracle samples. The answer meets user precision and recall targets with probability at least $1-δ$ for every workload and every catalog, so a stale or misleading view can cost oracle calls but never accuracy. On four workloads replayed against 725,000 recorded oracle labels, SemViews meets both targets on 99.63% of queries and saves 28%-45% of the oracle calls, whereas the only prior method in our study with the same guarantee needs 1.32x-1.71x as many calls. When a question returns in different words, views cut its calls by a further 27%-36%, with both targets met on at least 99.8% of such queries; similarity caches and entailment-based reuse meet them on only 17%-47%.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
This paper develops a smoothed generalized method of moments (GMM) framework for panel quantile models with individual-specific fixed-effects and endogenous regressors. By smoothing the indicator in the quantile moment conditions and profiling out the individual effects through smoothed individual quantile restrictions, the proposed estimator can be implemented using standard GMM algorithms. We establish consistency, asymptotic normality, and feasible inference under weak time dependence as both panel dimensions diverge. This dependence structure accommodates dynamic panel specifications, serially dependent disturbances, lagged instruments, and within-individual heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent inference. Monte Carlo simulations show that the estimator is nearly unbiased under endogeneity and yields generally accurate inference while remaining computationally tractable. An application to OECD inflation dynamics suggests asymmetric inflation propagation: under the structural IVQR interpretation, the response of current inflation to lagged inflation is substantially larger at the lower structural quantile than at the upper structural quantile.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting teacher representations of masked regions from visible context. Point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation that the context does not resolve. We call this constraint predictability bias. In computed tomography (CT), recurrent anatomy is predictable from context, whereas the sporadic, localized pathology that determines clinical interpretation often is not. We introduce TAP-JEPA, a ViT-B/3D trained on 113,611 CT volumes that is competitive with state-of-the-art encoders (COLIPRI, Merlin, VoxelFM) in scan-level classification. We then audit the learned predictive pathway by replaying the exact masking, teacher, and predictor computations used during training. Prediction lowers the mean Skill (prevalence-normalized average precision) from 0.388 to 0.271 for pathology, but only from 0.921 to 0.873 for anatomy. Along the teacher direction, separating pathology from matched control regions in the same organ, prediction moves pathology 34.7% toward the controls and controls 13.6% toward pathology, with larger shifts farther from visible context. Replacing visible matched-control representations increases surrounding-target prediction loss more than fully replacing pathology representations across four pathology categories. Downstream, removing all final-layer pathology tokens reduces the decision margin by at most 0.45% in four of seven scan-level probes. Together, these results show that contextual predictability is not a sufficient proxy for clinical relevance in medical representation learning. Training objectives should therefore retain diagnostic features regardless of their predictability from surrounding anatomy.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Local projections (LPs) have become a standard tool for estimating dynamic effects in macroeconomics and are typically implemented using ordinary least squares (OLS) for a given lag order. We propose an alternative approach that exploits additional lags as excluded instrumental variables (IVs). Under a finite-order model with martingale-difference shocks, the resulting (optimally weighted) IV estimator is never asymptotically less efficient than OLS and, as we show, can deliver substantial efficiency gains when data are persistent. For the unit-root AR(1) data with i.i.d. errors, our baseline IV estimator (with one overidentifying restriction) has asymptotic variance $2-h^{-1}$, compared with $h$, the asymptotic variance of the OLS lag-augmented estimator in Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Møller (2021), for an integer propagation horizon $h$. We then develop IV-based LP inference that is robust to unknown persistence and moderate local model misspecification, whereas the recursive VAR-based inference is generally not robust to the latter. We also characterize the trade-off between the degree of misspecification and the number of additional lag controls. Through simulations and an empirical application, we demonstrate that the proposed method can yield meaningfully shorter confidence intervals for impulse responses than OLS in finite samples.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Developmental dyslexia (DLX) affects 5-12% of the global population and impairs learning to read. Its biological basis, particularly the difficulties observed in oral phonological tasks, remains debated. Entrainment, the coupling of brain oscillations to speech rhythms, is essential for encoding phonological representations. We investigated whether brain entrainment to non-speech rhythms could predict DLX in 48 participants listening to white noise amplitude-modulated at rates matching Spanish speech units. Phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) signals yielded accurate DLX prediction for the 40 Hz stimulus using the Heights Ratio PAC measure (balanced accuracy 0.929, p = 0.0069, in the best case), indicating a stronger phonemic entrainment deficit in dyslexic individuals. Regression analysis in control (CTL) participants showed a strong dependence between reading performance scores and greater entrainment in language-associated brain regions. In particular, participants with poorer phonemic awareness, reading comprehension, or rapid automatized naming showed greater right-hemisphere entrainment to the 40 Hz stimulus. This finding adds evidence for the hemispheric compensatory mechanisms hypothesized in the literature. In conclusion, our methodology identifies dyslexia-specific entrainment patterns near language-associated brain regions, together with compensatory entrainment in right-hemisphere areas.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Metaheuristic comparisons are often reported at evaluation budgets far larger than an expensive engineering simulation can afford. This paper presents REMBGO, an evaluation-budget-aware refinement of EMBGO. Its contribution is not any single operator: it is the integration of population preservation, scale-normalized exploration and recovery mechanisms whose parent-relative benefit is concentrated under restricted function-evaluation budgets. REMBGO is evaluated on CEC2022 at a primary, application-aligned budget of 1040 function evaluations, with a surrounding budget ladder reported descriptively to characterise budget dependence rather than as a family of controlled hypotheses. A component-removal study finds no individual mechanism whose removal survives multiplicity correction, consistent with an integrated rather than a single-operator contribution. Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Targeted vaccination often prioritizes individuals who contribute most to transmission. However, this rationale may change under leaky protection, whereby vaccination reduces susceptibility at each exposure rather than fully preventing infection. Here, we use a survey-derived individual-level exposure framework for 2,279 residents to simulate infection dynamics across ranges of transmission intensity and vaccine efficacy. We compare two vaccination strategies: the high-exposure strategy (prioritizing highly exposed individuals) and the oldest-first strategy (prioritizing older individuals). As transmission intensity changes, we identify three patterns in the relative advantages of these two strategies. At low transmission, the high-exposure strategy outperforms the oldest-first strategy in reducing both epidemic peak size and final infection proportion. At intermediate transmission, it lowers epidemic peak size but increases final infection proportion, revealing a trade-off between these metrics. At high transmission, differences between the strategies narrow, and the oldest-first strategy has a slight advantage for both metrics. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of considering vaccine failure mode when evaluating vaccination policies under different transmission dynamics.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Prediction-market prices combine traders' judgments about future outcomes, but their errors may be concentrated in particular price ranges and change as settlement approaches. Prior cross-category evidence shows that Polymarket weather markets have larger pricing bias than other major categories, without separating low-price longshots from high-price favorites. This study compares the two ranges at different horizons in daily maximum-temperature markets. Event-level probability scores, cubic B-spline recalibration, and Buy-NO tests are used to examine the form and effect of the bias. Longshot overpricing mainly occurs at distant horizons, whereas favorite overpricing becomes much stronger during the final 1-12 hours and is nearly one order of magnitude larger. Event-level scores improve toward the daily temperature peak, while simple recalibration yields no statistically significant gains. The Buy-NO results in the corresponding time windows also show that the main pricing error is concentrated at the favorite end.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Data deduplication relies on content-defined chunking (CDC) algorithms to decide where data is split. We observe that most CDC algorithms are modular: a base chunking algorithm fixes the byte-level cut-point condition, while high-level techniques (size normalization, min/max thresholds, caching) layer on top. Existing benchmarks conflate the two, obscuring which design choices actually drive performance. We isolate and evaluate eight state-of-the-art base chunking algorithms across four realistic workloads and four metrics: throughput, deduplication ratio, mean chunk size, and chunk-size variance. Further, we derive new formulas relating algorithm parameters to expected chunk size for AE, RAM, and MII. In doing so, we uncover a longstanding error in the widely-used AE parameterization reproduced across multiple papers and evaluation tools that produces chunks 13-39% smaller than intended and inflates AE's reported deduplication. Across our evaluation, AE is the most balanced base chunking algorithm across all four metrics, RAM's similarity to AE does not carry over to low-entropy data, and MII and PCI show limited advantages over simpler alternatives in storage-oriented workloads. We release all implementations, datasets, and analysis scripts as open source.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Expressing ML algorithms as recursive aggregate SQL queries over distributed systems enables large-scale declarative data analytics, yet no existing system supports scalable provenance capture, necessary for ML explainability. We present ProvQML, a provenance-aware recursive aggregate SQL engine that efficiently captures fine-grained provenance while evaluating ML algorithms as recursive aggregate queries. We capture two types of provenance: (i) local provenance that records the contribution of each training instance to gradient computation at a specific model state, and (ii) global provenance that encodes the sequence of model parameter updates across the iterations. Extensive experiments on widely used ML datasets demonstrate that our approach efficiently captures both provenance for various ML models over widely used ML datasets.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Wireless capsule endoscopy is constrained by severe limitations in size, available power, and reliable data transmission through biological tissues. Although recent advances in miniature imaging sensors have improved image quality, the wireless transmission of color images at practical frame rates remains a challenging task under the tight capsule constraints. We present the design and the experimental validation of a miniaturized Wireless Imaging Transfer (WIT) system for capsule endoscopy based on a sub-GHz IEEE 802.11ah (Wi-Fi HaLow) wireless link. In addition, a preliminary in-vivo validation of Wi-Fi HaLow communication is reported, showing that a stable through-body wireless link can be established across biological tissues in a clinically relevant porcine model. These in-vivo results provide direct experimental support for the adoption of sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow for capsule endoscopy applications. Experimental results demonstrate stable wireless image transmission at a resolution of 320x320 pixels, with measured end-to-end data rates above 12 Mbps and a transmission energy efficiency of 20.7 nJ/bit. We also report a detailed power consumption analysis, with a breakdown of the contributions from the imaging sensor, illumination, digital processing, and RF transmission. When all active subsystem contributions are considered, including the camera, digital processing, RF transmission, and illumination at 60% LED brightness, the total power consumption is approximately 477 mW, corresponding to a complete-chain energy consumption of approximately 39.6 nJ/bit. Overall, the measured performance confirms that sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow provides a promising trade-off among throughput, robustness, and energy efficiency for wireless imaging in capsule endoscopy.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Clinical sleep medicine repeatedly documents profound divergences between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment, notably exemplified by sleep state misperception in paradoxical insomnia and boundary instability in narcolepsy type 1. Here, we present DyssomniaNN: a multi-scale biophysical computational framework coupling Borbély's two-process regulation of sleep homeostasis and circadian drive with Saper's hypothalamic reciprocal flip-flop circuit and a recurrent corticothalamic leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neural network. We formalize five clinical cohorts across an identical 72-hour photoperiod: healthy control, circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (delayed-phase), chronic insomnia, paradoxical insomnia, and narcolepsy type 1. The synthetic local field potential converges closely with empirical human electroencephalography spectra from the PhysioNet Sleep-EDF database across all canonical frequency bands (spectral mean absolute error of 0.33--0.35). Furthermore, we introduce the Well-Rested Index to quantify restorative efficacy. Simulations reveal that sleep duration fails to predict restorative recovery: paradoxical insomnia achieves normal total sleep time (21.15 h) yet yields low restoration (37.6%) from unsuppressed cortical beta-band intrusion, whereas hypocretin deficiency in narcolepsy produces severe nocturnal fragmentation (781 min of wake after sleep onset) and 35 sleep-onset rapid eye movement periods. DyssomniaNN provides an in silico platform for mechanistic sleep research and virtual neuropharmacology.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Accurate artery extraction from X-ray coronary angiography (XCA) is essential for coronary artery disease diagnosis and intervention. However, low vessel visibility, respiratory and cardiac motion, and limited annotations challenge existing methods. Moreover, most deep learning approaches produce binary vessel masks without preserving clinically relevant intra-arterial contrast information. We propose a Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model (TDBM) that formulates vessel extraction as image translation and learns from physics-informed synthetic data without manual vessel annotations. A physics-based XCA synthesis engine generates diverse, perfectly aligned pairs of contrast-enhanced and contrast-free images. Using these pairs, TDBM learns cross-domain mappings to recover high-fidelity vessel information. Temporal conditioning incorporates adjacent frames to improve consistency, while a vessel-aware contrastive loss exploits background-invariant synthetic pairs to enhance vascular discrimination. We evaluate TDBM on two XCA vessel segmentation datasets and conduct a reader study using two real-patient XCA sequence datasets. Zero-shot segmentation is further assessed on retinal imaging and fluorescence microscopy datasets. Results demonstrate that TDBM consistently outperforms existing methods and generalizes effectively across imaging modalities. Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Image-level MRI harmonization is often evaluated with a frozen site probe, a site classifier trained on raw scans and applied unchanged to harmonized ones: a drop in its accuracy is read as removal of site effects. We audit this practice on ABIDE I (1,112 T1-weighted scans, 17 sites) with ten output sets from seven harmonization methods and controls for chance, head shape, intensity, preprocessing and target alignment. We find that this verdict depends on how the probe is trained, even among probes that classify raw scans well: across random seeds, its balanced accuracy on the same CycleGAN outputs ranges from 0.13 to 0.59 (chance: 0.06). Low frozen-probe accuracy can also arise without harmonization: a Gaussian blur, which increases the intensity distance to the target site, lowers this accuracy to chance. Moreover, where the frozen probe fails, probes trained on the harmonized scans still recover the site, even from intensity histograms alone: on HACA3 outputs, the frozen probe scores 0.25, a probe trained on those outputs 0.75, and one using only their intensity histograms 0.71. Low frozen-probe accuracy therefore does not show that site information has been removed. We recommend reporting several probes trained to convergence, probes trained on harmonized scans, and target alignment.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Patient-level ultrasound diagnosis demands not only high predictive accuracy but also clinically aligned mitigation of asymmetric diagnostic risks. While Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) effectively models routine multi-view exams, standard aggregators often dilute heterogeneous diagnostic cues and optimize solely for global accuracy. This frequently yields undesirable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs. To bridge this gap, we propose C$^2$LUE, a novel MIL framework coupling evidence aware aggregation with risk-aligned regularization. To preserve evidence heterogeneity and prevent unimodal attention collapse, C$^2$LUE employs a multi-query cross-attention mechanism built upon a LoRA-adapted DINOv3 backbone. Multiple latent queries explicitly extract and disentangle diverse morphological patterns from the ultrasound sequence. Furthermore, to improve clinical risk alignment, we introduce a dynamic trade-off regularization objective that penalizes sensitivity-specificity imbalance during training. Rather than leaving the clinical trade-off entirely to post-hoc threshold adjustment, this objective encourages the learned score distribution toward a more balanced operating region. Extensive evaluations on patient-level, biopsy-proven thyroid and breast ultrasound datasets demonstrate that C$^2$LUE consistently outperforms prior alternatives. By uniting strong discrimination with a balanced error profile, C$^2$LUE provides a promising solution for real-world ultrasound screening and diagnosis.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Gate coefficients describe how a fusion layer weights intermediate features, but they do not necessarily reflect the magnitude of branch contributions at the classifier output. We investigate this distinction in a fixed 3D MedVAE--radiomics model for clear cell versus non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification from contrast-enhanced CT. Because the model uses a linear classification head, the binary decision logit can be decomposed exactly into a gated image term, a direct radiomics term, and a bias. We define effective radiomics dominance as the direct radiomics term's share of the summed absolute non-bias branch contributions and compare it with structural radiomics weighting. Internally, mean structural radiomics weighting was 0.823, whereas mean effective radiomics dominance was 0.148, with a modest case-wise association (\r{ho} = 0.290). The gated image term retained substantially stronger discriminative ranking information than the direct radiomics term. The same structural-to-effective discrepancy was observed in exploratory external evaluation. Branch-targeted permutation, integrated-gradient, and Shapley-style analyses further identified radiomics descriptors influencing the direct radiomics term. Because radiomics also generates the gate, the gated image term remains radiomics-dependent, so additive branch contribution should not be interpreted as total input influence. These findings show that structural gate weighting and decision-level branch contribution represent distinct aspects of gated feature fusion and should be interpreted separately.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Many large enterprise and cloud deployments rely on metrics observability solutions (e.g., Prometheus) to monitor key performance indicators of system health (e.g., CPU, memory, network, app-level statistics). Monitoring and analyzing these metrics presents a significant challenge in terms of cost-latency tradeoffs at scale. Ideally, system operators would like immediately deployable and backwards compatible solutions to improve the cost-latency tradeoffs without significant impact on the fidelity of their observability applications. Unfortunately, existing solutions including state-of-art timeseries databases and custom approximate querying solutions fail on one or more aspects. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of TurboProm, a backwards-compatible drop-in accelerator for metrics observability deployments. TurboProm recasts metrics analytics tasks using a semantic-preserving summary view rather than classical query-centric view. Instead of estimating query results on raw timeseries metrics data, TurboProm uses semantic-preserving summaries that enable high-fidelity analytics with significant cost-latency improvements. We present a practical implementation of TurboProm that can be retrofitted to any existing observability deployment. We evaluate TurboProm on diverse real and synthetic workloads against state-of-art solutions and show that it can provide significant reduction in query latency and cost. TurboProm is open-source at https://github.com/ProjectASAP/ASAPQuery.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
This article presents an electronic experimental validation of discontinuity-induced bifurcations, including period-adding cascades, in a wake-induced dynamical system subjected to soft impacts. A cylindrical structure immersed in a cross-flow undergoes vortex-induced vibrations and interacts with a movable barrier during the upper and lower branches of the response. The structural motion is modelled as a harmonic oscillator, while the fluctuating lift is represented by a Van der Pol oscillator. The soft contact interaction between the structure and the movable barrier is modelled using a bilinear restoring force, resulting in a piecewise-smooth wake-oscillator system. A systematic numerical investigation reveals period-adding cascades of periodic orbits interspersed with chaotic responses as the barrier distance and fluid-flow velocity are varied. The results are experimentally validated using an inductorless electronic analogue of the piecewise-smooth wake model constructed from operational amplifiers and implemented on a printed-circuit board to improve experimental robustness. The route to instability of the periodic and aperiodic responses is further characterized using Floquet multipliers and Lyapunov exponents. A zero-time transverse discontinuity mapping is implemented to account for the evolution of perturbations in the local neighborhood of the discontinuity boundary during stability analysis. The combined numerical, experimental, and stability analyses demonstrate the role of soft impacts in generating complex nonlinear responses in the wake-induced system.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We investigate signal transmission in a one-dimensional chain of $n$ locally coupled plasma oscillators with asymmetric bidirectional coupling $(ε_1,ε_2)$. Our results reveal a clear contrast between symmetric and asymmetric interactions: while symmetric coupling suppresses signal propagation, coupling asymmetry enables efficient nonlinear transmission across the network. In particular, sustained long range transmission is achieved when the forward coupling strength exceeds the backward coupling strength ($ε_1 > ε_2$), as demonstrated through a comprehensive phase diagram in the $(ε_1,ε_2)$ parameter space. Furthermore, under asymmetric diffusive coupling, signal transmission can persist even when the first few oscillators in the chain undergo oscillation death. A central finding of this study is the intrinsic generation of higher harmonics induced by nonlinear interactions, leading to a pronounced reversal of vibrational resonance. This nonlinear redistribution of energy facilitates selective amplification and robust propagation of specific frequency components.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We investigate signal transmission in a network of unidirectionally coupled plasma oscillators, where only the first oscillator is driven by a weak periodic input. As the signal propagates through the network, nonlinear interactions generate higher-order harmonic components. Spectral analysis identifies five distinct transmission patterns for the fundamental frequency and odd harmonics, and four patterns for even harmonics, encompassing damped propagation, undamped transmission, and localized amplification. The transmission characteristics are governed by both the coupling strength and system parameters. Furthermore, we analyze how variations in these key parameters shape the overall signal dynamics.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Invasive alien species (IAS) generate substantial ecological and economic damages that often transcend political boundaries, creating strong incentives for coordinated management. We develop a two-region ecological-economic model of IAS control that integrates prevention and eradication measures with population dynamics characterized by logistic growth and an Allee effect. We derive analytical results on the interaction between ecological thresholds and strategic behaviour and compare outcomes under cooperation (central planner) and non-cooperation (open loop Nash equilibrium and Markovian Nash equilibrium). We show that, under realistic control costs, neither prevention nor eradication can eliminate invasive populations in finite time, and complete prevention of cross-border spread is generally not optimal. In the absence of an Allee effect, the zero-population equilibrium is unstable, implying long-run persistence of the invasive species. By contrast, the presence of an Allee effect fundamentally alters system dynamics by making extinction locally stable and creating a basin of attraction within which eradication becomes feasible. This finding highlights the economic significance of ecological thresholds and demonstrates how delays in management can shift populations beyond critical levels, after which eradication is unlikely regardless of subsequent control efforts. Numerical simulations further show that cooperative management expands the set of initial conditions leading to eradication and consistently reduces aggregate social costs relative to decentralized management. The results provide a formal rationale for rapid intervention, precautionary regulation, and stronger multilateral cooperation in IAS management, particularly in jurisdictions such as the European Union where listing and control actions may be delayed pending evidence of harm.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We develop a dynamical mean-field framework for the full finite-time and stationary asymptotic Lyapunov spectra of random recurrent neural networks. At finite observation time, an exact log-determinant representation of tangent-propagator singular values leads to a closed-contour matrix Dyson equation for the smoothed spectral tail. In the stationary setting, a cocycle representation yields an operator equation for the asymptotic cumulative spectrum. Both formulations retain complete local gain histories and the repeated action of quenched connectivity. Direct singular-value calculations and network QR spectra support the predictions in the regimes examined, with sampling uncertainty and numerical cutoffs assessed separately. The stationary equation also recovers the known maximal exponent, and controlled gain-history replay illustrates how temporal correlations redistribute instability. This work was carried out in collaboration with ChatGPT 5.6 Sol. Toward the end of preparation we became aware of David G. Clark's contemporaneous work, \emph{Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks}[arXiv:2610.12426], which reports overlapping mean-field results for the full Lyapunov spectrum using a cavity approach.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Production vector search must continuously ingest, delete, and re-tenant vectors while serving low-latency, high-recall, metadata-filtered approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) queries for many tenants with per-tenant service-level objectives. Existing graph-based ANN systems address these requirements largely in isolation, leaving recall during concurrent re-optimization without an analytical bound. We develop a graph-based index that combines streaming updates, filtered search, and multi-tenancy, with one theoretical result and two system mechanisms. Our theory decomposes per-tenant recall loss into staleness from updates not yet integrated into the graph and filtered navigability determined by the local density of points satisfying a tenant's predicate. The staleness component exhibits anti-amortization on a merge-based graph, integrating a larger batch of inserts increases recall degradation super-linearly, so larger merges do not reduce total staleness loss. Holding the insert horizon fixed while increasing merge size 20x, we observe a monotonic decrease in terminal recall@10 from 99.44% to 99.01%. For filtered search, the theory gives a parameter-free frontier-mass relationship in local predicate density and a query-averaged per-tenant recall bound. We instantiate the bound with a filter and tenant-aware staging cache and a select-not-resize scheduler with per-tenant staleness ceilings. On a FreshDiskANN substrate, the ceiling eliminates tight-tier SLA violations under the evaluated churn workload, while merge reordering changes terminal recall by only 0.02 percentage points. The results show how recall bounds can guide background maintenance without relying on merge resizing as a recall control mechanism.

This paper extends the finite-population asymptotic framework of Abadie et al. (2014,2020) to the generalized method of moments (GMM) estimator for moment condition models. Motivating examples include instrumental variable regressions and regression adjustments under randomized controlled trials. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the GMM estimator and propose conservative variance estimators. We also study GMM weighting, misspecification, and over-identification testing under finite-population asymptotics. Notably, even though the optimally weighted GMM estimator is infeasible under finite-population asymptotics, the regression adjustment estimator in a randomized controlled trial is shown to be asymptotically equivalent to the optimally weighted GMM estimator. A simulation study and real data application illustrate the usefulness of our GMM theory.

We highlight the connection between structure-specific dynamic programming algorithms and the mathematical enumeration of the possible merge trees from a join graph. We present two case studies, on double-star and helix shaped join graphs, that we believe carry useful techniques for a toolbox of building structure-specific join optimizers. For the double-star case, we show how the enumeration leads directly to a significantly improved search algorithm, whereas for the helix case we show that a algorithm derived from the mathematical enumeration is not necessarily better than structure-agnostic algorithms.

In this work we present a model of a neuroglivascular unit associated with a neuronal ensemble. We combine calcium dynamics in the astrocyte, the cascade of synthesis of arachidonic acid and its derivatives, as well as the activity of the network of inhibitory and excitatory neurons with changes in local blood flow. We add equations to the model for extracellular neurotransmitters such as GABA, glutamate, and norepinephrine. Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Does evolutionary entropy depend on the width of the age classes used to describe a population? We show that the apparent dependence on temporal resolution is a consequence of the loss of information about reproductive timing within discrete classes. When this information is retained, corresponding continuous and discrete representations yield the same cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential in a common unit of time. When within-class timing is unknown, a uniform local reconstruction yields a logarithmic correction. For constant post-maturity hazard and fertility, continuous exponential and discrete geometric descriptions correspond exactly at every time scale. Thus, for a fixed reference duration, evolutionary entropy is a property of the reproductive process, not of its temporal partition. These results provide a mathematical basis for comparing demographic models across different temporal scales by identifying the information required to separate differences in reproductive organisation from effects of the chosen age-class representation.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
What makes natural languages diversify, in their syntactic structure, even when sharing a largely common origin? We refine our simple model, which focuses on the glassy dynamics induced by a network of interactions between syntactic parameters. Distinguishing between symmetric interaction weights that can be inferred from the observed statistics of syntax across many languages, and additional asymmetric weights assigned at random, we show that both components are needed, with similar overall strength, to account for plausible long-term syntactic dynamics. An approximate balance can combine the glassy metastability provided by the inferred weights with the chaotic diversification induced by the residual asymmetric weights.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Researchers and policymakers frequently make a large number of decisions simultaneously over many units using noisy estimates of unit-level effects. Researchers often assume that unit-level effects are drawn from a common effect distribution, allowing for optimal decision-making. In applications, however, this effect distribution is unknown to the econometrician, introducing uncertainty in the ultimate decision-making problem. This paper considers the problem of quantifying this uncertainty. For instance, researchers may seek to understand how an oracle decision maker with knowledge of the effect distribution would compare different feasible decisions, or understand which decisions an oracle would plausibly make. Analyzing these questions from the perspective of an oracle decision maker involves comparing the conditional means of unit-level effects given estimates thereof, suggesting a sufficient inferential objective of uniform coverage of these conditional means. Based on an equivalence between uniform coverage of conditional means and multiple testing, I develop methods that satisfy this coverage. Finally, I consider an application to the problem of identifying high-economic-mobility neighborhoods. My methods sharpen inference relative to existing methods and identify units that can be confidently included in oracle selections.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) has been the dominant concurrency protocol in modern database management systems (DBMSs). However, cloud-native HTAP architectures shift many of MVCC's traditional advantages from the primary transaction engine to the deployment architecture. Now, transactional and analytical processing are decoupled into loosely synchronized engines, while cloud deployment primitives provide the workload isolation required for this design. In this paper, we challenge the status quo, arguing that single-version concurrency control (SVCC) is better suited to cloud transaction processing than MVCC. Through a systematic analysis of MVCC's limitations, we show that SVCC avoids these shortcomings through a more lightweight and efficient design. Beyond arguing for a lighter transaction processing, we use this SVCC effort as a blueprint to advocate for a broader rethinking of cloud-native architectures and to outline a research roadmap to shape next-generation DBMSs.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Automatic extraction and anatomical numbering (R01-R12, L01-L12) of all 24 rib centerlines in thoracic CT is essential for unfolded rib visualization, fracture detection, and surgical navigation, but remains challenging due to adjacent-bone confluence, calcified costal cartilage bridges, kyphotic pose variation, and partial visibility of terminal ribs. We present ribline, an open-source three-stage framework combining: (1) an automatically detected lung-apex and vertebral-midline coordinate frame with a kyphosis-aware azimuthal angle for point ordering along each rib; (2) a hybrid voxel detector fusing an anatomically anchored Semantic Context Forest (SCF) with a lightweight 3D U-Net; and (3) a global stage that decomposes the probability skeleton into candidate curves, assigns rib indices via a bilateral Viterbi dynamic program coupled across both hemithoraces, and refines curves via template recovery and normal-plane centering (RibSnake). On the Siemens Corporate Research 2 mm thoracic CT benchmark (47 training and 12 evaluation scans), our pipeline achieves a labeled Chamfer distance of 2.05 mm, labeled clDice of 0.886 (3 mm) and 0.945 (4 mm), 97.2% labeling accuracy (278/286 ribs), and zero false-positive curves on the evaluation split, and 3.64 mm (median 2.39 mm) with 91.8% labeling accuracy across all 59 annotated scans (1,402 ribs) in 5-fold cross-validation. Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We argue that tacit knowing is better modelled as an operating regime of a memory than as a kind of content. Our substrate is VaCoAl, an algebro-deterministic XOR-and-shift hyperdimensional memory over GF(2), realized as CASRAM and PyVaCoAl. In it, a DAG reads two ways. Repairing every collision (Rescue) makes the trace exactly auditable but ranks no path higher; tolerating them (Don't Care) yields a path confidence, CR$_2$, silently favouring direct routes. This audit-valuation complementarity formalizes Polanyi's claim that tacit and explicit are not sharply divided. It separates contingent tacitness, which a new query brings out (AlphaGo's game tree), from regime-bound tacitness, statable only once it is gone (AlphaGo's hunches). (1) Polanyi's from-to structure reads as non-commutative binding. (2) Explicating the valuation destroys it, as with Polanyi's pianist, yet a closed-form law states it. Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins each capture part of this, narrowly; even Nonaka and von Krogh's continuum cannot tell the classes apart. (3) Collins's three tacit knowledges become strata, one outside the substrate. (4) Our mentor-student DAG is a tacit-transmission graph. (5) Tao's remark that AI-solved problems spawn few follow-ups reveals rootless explicit knowledge: checkable results no one can trace or yet understands. Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Recent advances in foundation models and large-scale cellular perturbation datasets have driven growing interest in using LLMs to predict and reason about cellular responses. Biological reasoning in this setting involves relating molecular mechanisms, cellular responses, and functional outcomes across scales. Evaluating foundation models therefore requires assessing not only whether their predictions are correct, but also how those predictions depend on the biological evidence provided. We introduce CellChain, an experimentally grounded benchmark comprising 590 biological cases and 2,360 matched evidence-condition instances across gene-dependency prediction, cytokine-axis identification, and drug-sensitivity ranking. CellChain links perturbation experiments and external biological resources through a provenance-aware evidence graph spanning molecular, pathway, transcriptional, and phenotypic information. Task-specific conditions vary evidence coverage, composition, or assignment while preserving questions, candidate answers, reference targets, and scoring rules. Across 18 foundation models, the highest accuracies under prespecified target-evidence conditions are 57.5%, 75.5%, and 70.8%, respectively, and broader evidence coverage does not consistently improve accuracy. On the drug-sensitivity benchmark cohort, matched reference histories outperform swapped histories by an average of 13.0 percentage points in cluster-weighted accuracy. Decision-transition analysis separates corrections, newly introduced errors, and wrong-answer switches, revealing substantial answer changes hidden by small net accuracy differences. CellChain provides controlled comparisons for attributing changes in model predictions to prespecified expansions of biological context, including changes in evidence coverage, composition, and biological assignment.

We present an overview of R package called \texttt{naspaclust}, a tool for spatial fuzzy clustering improvement by hybridising the Fuzzy Geographically Weighted Clustering (FGWC) with nature-inspired optimisation algorithms. There are seven optimisation algorithms in general, namely Artificial Bee Colony, Flower Pollination Algorithm, Gravitational Search Algorithm, Harris-Hawk Optimisation, Intelligent Firefly Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimisation, and Teaching-Learning Based optimisation. The optimisation algorithms available do not only use the basic algorithms, but also the modified version of several parts such as randomisation terms and updating rules. Furthermore, we also provide additional options by providing more distance metrics options based on the \texttt{ rdist} package. This study showed the implementation of the \texttt{naspaclust} package in various cases, as well as comparing the performance of the algorithms in the scope of basic algorithms. The \texttt{naspaclust} package allows to improve the performance of fuzzy clustering, mainly in spatial context.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
This paper investigates the geometric detection of latent dynamic transitions (where the latent space is defined as a finite-dimensional state space reconstructed via a delay-embedding Hankel matrix) in mutually coupled phase-locked loops (PLLs) exhibiting on-off intermittent chaos. We propose a data-driven approach to identify the transition of the effective dimension in latent dynamics as a precursor to physical bursting events. By applying Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to a Hankel matrix constructed from high-resolution oversampled data, we extract the effective dimension that reflects the dynamical shift of intrinsic variables - from a synchronized two-dimensional manifold to a higher-dimensional chaotic state - prior to the actual burst. This geometric indicator enables a proactive, event-driven intervention using Pyragas-type delayed feedback control, which is activated only when the detected dimension exceeds a critical threshold. Simulation results demonstrate that this geometric precursor effectively compensates for control latencies and substantially reduces accumulated control energy compared to conventional continuous feedback. The findings establish a methodological strategy for stabilizing infinite-dimensional delayed systems by exploiting early warning signals embedded in dimensional transitions of latent dynamics.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Surface-based cortical analysis is useful in many applications as it is a natural way to model the highly folded structure of the cerebral cortex, allowing quantities such as curvature and thickness to be easily calculated. Existing deep learning (DL) methods have focused on 1x1x1 mm3 T1-weighted (T1w) scans, thus replicating classical pipelines. Here we present a neural network that is trained exclusively on synthetic scans with random contrast and resolution. Consequently, it can be applied to almost any kind of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan. In addition, our model provides vertex-wise uncertainty estimates of the predicted surface as well as a spherical registration to fsaverage space. Our model performs on par with other state-of-the-art DL methods on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans and outperforms the only other method capable of estimating cortical surfaces from low resolution, non-T1w scans. The predicted uncertainty, moreover, correlates with overall scan quality on low resolution scans and highlights areas of poor surface reconstruction on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans, suggesting that it can be used for quality control. Finally, the predicted spherical registrations prove comparable to other DL and classical registration methods. These qualities, when combined with the fast inference time, will provide the ability to analyze large, existing databases of clinical MRI scans, with the potential for finding disease-specific patterns that would otherwise be infeasible in a research setting.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
This paper develops likelihood-based estimation for parametric rational inattention--additive random utility models. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the exact maximum likelihood estimator and provide conditions under which the simulated estimator shares its asymptotic distribution. To implement estimation, we develop Newton--BA, a KKT-guided hybrid of Newton--Raphson and Blahut--Arimoto (BA). The algorithm accommodates both interior and boundary solutions and substantially improves computational efficiency relative to direct BA while preserving numerical accuracy. Monte Carlo simulations show that parameter recovery improves with sample size and that confidence-interval coverage is generally close to the nominal $95$ percent level. Finally, we compare our model with no- and perfect-information logit benchmarks in an empirically calibrated ModeCanada experiment. Our model achieves similar in-sample likelihood fit to perfect-information logit but more accurately recovers key preference parameters, choice probabilities, and responses to travel-time changes.
