Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Engineering graduates in India enter a technology sector that is being reshaped by generative AI, yet the route into that sector runs through examinations and campus placement screens that largely exclude AI. Institutions in India have an approved intake of nearly 2.9 million seats in engineering and technology for 2026-2027, but HCI research on how students prepare for AI-mediated work has drawn mostly on Western and East Asian settings. We interviewed 23 students and recent graduates of Indian engineering and computing programmes about how they used generative AI across coursework, examinations and placements, and how they judged their own readiness for work. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we report five themes, covering AI-first workplaces and AI-free placement screens, how participants prepared for placement, how they used AI in coursework, the role of faculty authority and enforcement, and participants' concerns about their readiness for work. Drawing on signaling theory, we discuss what grades and screen scores certify once AI can help produce them, and we offer recommendations for employers, institutions and AI tool designers.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
When including covariates in Difference-in-Differences, researchers must consider not only which covariates to include, but also how to model them. The Common Causality of Covariates (CCC) assumption requires that covariate coefficients in the untreated potential-outcome model remain constant across regions and periods. Violations can bias DID estimators even when the relevant covariates are correctly included. I develop a CCC test based on Wald tests from an additive model that uses untreated observations in pre-treatment periods to assess whether covariate coefficients vary across regions, periods, or both. Motivated by this specification problem, I show theoretically that well-specified Integrated DID estimators are consistent, whereas overly restrictive models can introduce bias and, under conditional homoskedasticity, unnecessarily flexible models can reduce efficiency. Monte Carlo simulations show that the CCC test has good size and power. An application to private-sector Ban-the-Box policies finds variation across both regions and periods, with positive estimated effects on wages and occupational quality among employed private-sector workers.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Executing vision-language models (VLMs) aboard low-Earth orbit satellites enables flexible processing of observation data without first downlinking it to the ground. On commercial off-the-shelf payloads, however, a request may span multiple execution windows: power and thermal constraints, fault-triggered reboots, and competing payload demands can interrupt inference before it completes. Each shutdown discards volatile activations and KV caches, forcing an unprotected request to repeat work after restart. We present OrbitWeaver, a framework that preserves VLM inference progress across onboard interruptions through coordinated checkpointing and recovery. Its phase-aware checkpointing selects recovery boundaries according to the state lifetimes and computational characteristics of vision encoding, language-model prefill, and decoding, balancing storage traffic against recomputation. Its dependency-aware dynamic recovery schedules restoration from partially completed states across the layer and token-chunk dimensions. By overlapping checkpoint and weight reads with recomputation, it reduces restart latency; the recovery planner computes an optimal execution order under its scheduling model within 100 ms. Experiments on satellite payload hardware using on-orbit telemetry traces show up to a 4.07-fold end-to-end speedup and a 3.56-fold reduction in SSD write volume over the evaluated baselines. A 72-hour deployment on two low-Earth orbit satellites demonstrates that OrbitWeaver retains inference progress and resumes execution across repeated bus-enforced shutdowns.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study labeling schemes for $p \times q$ $Γ$-free binary matrices, which do not contain a submatrix of the form $Γ= \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$. We give a labeling scheme that uses $O(\log^2 N)$-bit labels for rows and columns, where $N=p+q$, such that any matrix entry can be determined from the corresponding two labels in constant time in the word RAM model. The worst-case label size matches the counting lower bound up to constant factors. We also show that the entrywise least $Γ$-free supermatrix of an arbitrary $p\times q$ binary matrix, together with its labels, can be constructed in $O(pq)$ time. Our construction represents a $Γ$-free matrix by a sequence of rooted forests, where each column corresponds to a node and the $1$-entries of each row form a root path in its corresponding forest. For $n$-vertex strongly chordal and chordal bipartite graphs, our result gives asymptotically optimal $O(\log^2 n)$-bit adjacency labeling schemes with constant-time queries. These results answer both representation questions posed by Spinrad in 1995.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive emergent reasoning capabilities, yet they remain constrained by fixed model parameters and finite context windows. Even when augmented with static retrieval, they can produce statements that are unsupported by, or even contradictory to, retrieved evidence. This leads to hallucinations, difficulty incorporating up-to-date information, and failures to correctly interpret or reconcile sources. Recent work addresses these limitations by tightly coupling step-by-step reasoning with interactive search, treating retrieval as an action within an iterative agentic loop rather than a one-shot preprocessing step. This study reviews frameworks that implement such reasoning-search loops by interleaving planning, querying, retrieval, integration, verification, and stopping. We analyze these systems through four architectural axes: retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge source, and grounding strictness. We separately treat the learning signal as a cross-cutting dimension because prompting, supervision, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning can instantiate the same architecture while producing materially different search, stopping, and grounding behavior. We further distinguish benchmark difficulty from RSA-loop demand and synthesize controlled within-study ablations and quality-cost deltas, avoiding invalid pooling across heterogeneous model backbones, retrievers, corpora, and evaluation protocols. Our goal is to clarify the landscape of reasoning-search-augmented LLMs and outline a unified perspective on the design choices shaping future research.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The fragmentation of a liquid jet in a crossflowing airstream arises from a complex interplay between aerodynamic forcing and interfacial instabilities acting across a wide range of length scales. We examine the spatial evolution of droplet size distributions along the jet trajectory using a combination of high-speed shadowgraphy and digital in-line holography, allowing simultaneous characterization of jet morphology and volumetric droplet size distributions. The results demonstrate a clear progression of breakup mechanisms, from near-field bag rupture to downstream rim, ligament, and node disintegration, each associated with distinct characteristic length scales. This evolution is reflected in the droplet size distributions, which broaden and become increasingly polydisperse downstream relative to the near-field distributions. By systematically varying the liquid-jet and airstream Weber numbers, we identify distinct breakup modes, and construct a regime map that delineates the column-breakup, isolated-bag-breakup, and interacting-bag regimes. Furthermore, by incorporating the dominant instability mechanisms, including Rayleigh-Taylor and Rayleigh-Plateau instabilities associated with the observed column, bag, and multi-bag breakup modes, we develop a theoretical framework for jet atomization in crossflow. The framework relates instability wavelengths to characteristic droplet sizes, and reasonably captures the experimentally observed trends. We found that stronger aerodynamic forcing induces earlier breakup, decreases the characteristic instability length scales, and generates finer droplets dispersed over a wider spatial region. Overall, the study establishes a quantitative relationship between instability-driven fragmentation dynamics and droplet size distributions, thereby connecting interfacial instabilities with measurable spray characteristics.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Neural network models are increasingly constructed from synapse-resolution connectomes, and the same circuit is now available in reconstructions from other animals and pipelines. We do not know whether such models are dependent on the reconstruction they are built from, and whether connectome differences are biological or measurement errors. We studied the Drosophila head-direction circuit in nine versions: four flies (male CNS, hemibrain, FlyWire, BANC) and five variants of the same fly varying only by thresholds, proofreading or synapse detection. Using wiring-based correspondences validated by anatomical labels, we place all differences on one scale. A change of synapse detection within one fly changed the circuit more than halfway to the smallest between-fly difference on four distance measures; proofreading differences were smaller but depended on the metric, and left and right halves of one fly differed no more than random halves. Networks trained on each wiring to hold a cued heading developed near-perfect ring attractors, but their error increased from below 1 degree to 10-28 degrees when all weights changed by 1%. Training on each wiring did not transfer to any other connectome, including other versions of the same fly; refitting thirty cell-type gains, we repaired filtering-level differences but remaining error depended on wiring distance. Training with noise lowered precision and gave only partial transfer. In imaging data, the fly compass drifted gradually in darkness. Connectome-constrained models should report the reconstruction they were built on and be tested for robustness across reconstructions.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Personalized shopping benchmarks ask which item fits the user; we ask how far an agent may commit on that item, and pose learning the individual's auto-purchase line as a task. The boundary is evidence-conditioned and three-valued: whether committing is appropriate depends on the sufficiency of product information (warrant), reversibility, price against the user's norm, and urgency, not only on fit; and the natural output is don't buy, confirm first, or buy automatically. Across sixteen instruction-tuned models, autonomous commitment is misaligned with a human authorization reference in which fifteen annotators, role-playing the delegating principal from a given profile, choose the furthest action they would allow without confirmation: models commit even when fit is low and when their own evidence flag reports the warrant missing. This is overreach. The line is individual: these raters disagree, yet the disagreement is structured and partly predictable from a person's own other labels. A shallow learner on a few dozen of a person's own labels predicts their held-out auto-purchase line at a median of 0.79 by 30-40 labels, outperforming every evaluated prompt$\times$model configuration, including a per-annotator oracle over 80 configurations; the learned boundary does not transfer across domains. We release the counterfactual benchmark, human authorization reference, and annotation protocol after acceptance.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Many policies determine social arrangements whose effects depend on the relationships formed afterwards. We study how to learn such policies when a constrained joint action changes network formation and outcomes depend on exposures to the resulting network. Policy value integrates an outcome response over the distribution of post-assignment networks. The large number of feasible arrangements makes it difficult to evaluate policies directly from historical data. We therefore adopt a model-based approach that pools information across assignments to evaluate alternative arrangements. We characterize identification of policy values and construct plug-in estimators. Our regret bounds account for sampling variation, first-stage estimation error, and computational errors. Our applications to classroom seating and business groups illustrate predicted welfare gains from learned rules relative to random assignment.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Retrieval-augmented generation over multi-viewpoint queries must preserve distinct answers and positions from the retrieved evidence while operating under a fixed context budget. We introduce LMVU, a lightweight ranker that learns to prioritize candidates by the marginal viewpoint coverage they add to the current selection. Training uses viewpoint annotations from each benchmark's development split to compare candidates within the same selection state. At inference, LMVU repeatedly scores budget-feasible candidates as the context grows, without accessing these annotations. We evaluate two forms of recovered viewpoint coverage: RVC$_1$ assigns each viewpoint full credit for at least one supporting source unit, while RVC$_2$ assigns half credit for one and full credit for two or more distinct source units. Exact oracles measure achievable coverage under the same evidence pool and budget. Across four viewpoint-annotated benchmarks at a 1,024-token budget, LMVU achieves gains of up to 0.047 and 0.052 points in RVC$_1$ and RVC$_2$, respectively, over the strongest non-oracle baseline for each benchmark and metric, and reaches the exact viewpoint-breadth ceiling on two benchmarks.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The bulk-boundary correspondence establishes a fundamental connection between bulk band topology and the emergence of boundary states, underpinning topological phenomena across electronic, acoustic, photonic, and many other wave systems. A broad class of singular flatband systems, however, exhibits an unconventional form of bulk-boundary correspondence, in which robust boundary modes (RBMs) originate from flatband-touching points (FBTPs) and the real-space topology associated with incomplete sets of compact localized states (CLSs), rather than conventional momentum-space bulk topological invariants. To date, experimental studies of such boundary modes have been limited to systems hosting lower-order FBTPs. Here, we experimentally demonstrate unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence in a photonic cross-bedded Kagome-like lattice featuring a higher-order FBTP formed by the touching of two degenerate flatbands and a dispersive band. Using continuous-wave laser writing, we observe shape-preserving propagation of both bulk CLSs and boundary RBMs. Remarkably, unlike previously reported flatband systems, the RBMs retain their boundary localization under input-field perturbations involving both singular and nonsingular CLSs, revealing an unconventional boundary response associated with the higher-order FBTP in this lattice. Our results establish the Kagome-like lattice as a new platform for exploring flatband physics and unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, with potential applications in wave localization, flatband lasers, and other emerging topological photonic devices.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:

For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_δ$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_δ$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study Largest Cardinality Subset Sum (LCSS): given $n$ nonnegative integers and a target $t$, compute a subset summing to $t$ with maximum cardinality. We also consider its all-targets version (ATLCSS), which asks for this maximum for every sum $s\in\{1,\ldots,t\}$. The LCSS problem sits squarely between the subset sum and the knapsack problem. A straightforward dynamic-programming algorithm runs in time $O(nt)$ and solves ATLCSS, and using Jin and Bringmann (both in STOC 2024, independent work) $0$-$1$ knapsack results we achieve a $\widetilde{O}(n + a_{\max}^2)$-time deterministic algorithm for LCSS. Our main result is a randomized $\widetilde{O}(n+\sqrt{n}\,t)$-time algorithm for LCSS. Then, we complement this result with a randomized $\widetilde{O}(n+t^{3/2})$-time algorithm for ATLCSS. Together, our two algorithms give a $\widetilde{O}(n+t\min\{\sqrt{n},\sqrt{t}\})$-time algorithm for LCSS. As an application of ATLCSS, we solve the search version of Projection Subset Sum, introduced by Dutta and Rajasree (SYNSAC 2023), in $\widetilde{O}(n+t^{3/2})$ time for every fixed $\ell_p$ norm with $p\geq 1$. For $\ell_1$, we obtain $\widetilde{O}(n+t)$ time, removing the unique-representation assumption required by their algorithm. Both algorithms output an optimal modified vector and a witnessing subset.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The Fréchet distance (also known as the dog-leash distance) is a well-studied and prevalent distance measure for polygonal curves. In this paper we present parallel algorithms for computing the discrete \frechet\ distance between two curves, in both the PRAM and MPC models. For two polygonal curves of length $n$, we show that the distance between them can be computed in the PRAM model in $O(\log n/ σ)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{2+σ})$ total work for any $0<σ<1$. In the sublinear MPC model with $n^ρ$ space per machine, it can be computed in $O(\log n / ρ^2)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{2+ρ})$ total space. For $c$-packed curves, we match our bounds to the sequential algorithms, showing that a $(1+\eps)$-approximation of the distance can be computed in the PRAM model in $O(\log{n}+1/σ^3)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{1+σ})$ total work, and in the sublinear MPC model in $O(1 /ρ^3)$ rounds and $\tilde{O}(n^{1+ρ})$ total space, for any constant $\eps>0$. As part of our algorithms for $c$-packed curves, we also present parallel algorithms for computing curve simplifications, which may be of independent interest.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ranking. We prove that exact autobidding equilibria under budget and return-on-investment (ROI) constraints can be computed in polynomial time whenever either the number $n$ of advertisers or the number $K$ of display slots is fixed. Our algorithms rely on two structural reductions. With few advertisers, the payment polytopes of tied bid layers combine by a Minkowski sum, giving a fixed-dimensional representation of exponentially many rankings. With few slots, budget equilibria admit threshold recovery and an exact submodular description of attainable payments at the display boundary. For ROI, we prove that every group-consecutive equilibrium has a representative with at most $K+2$ nonunit multipliers, preserving the item and price in every displayed slot. In each case, the reduction leads to polynomially many systems of polynomial equations and inequalities in bounded dimension. The algorithms compute exact multipliers and explicit distributions over valid group-consecutive rankings, with support at most $n+1$; for ROI with few slots, this improves to $\min\{n+1,K+3\}$.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Mass transfer (MT) in binary systems is a crucial and complex process. Even before the donor's photosphere fills its Roche lobe, matter from its outer atmosphere can reach the inner Lagrange point, thus initiating interaction in the so-called optically thin phase. Most existing models account for a very tenuous atmosphere supported by thermal gas pressure, thus predicting very little MT until the donor fills its Roche lobe. However, recent hydrodynamic simulations of giant stars suggest that shock-driven outflows can create substantially thicker "chromospheres'' extending to a few stellar radii. In this work, we derive a simple analytic model for a shock-supported chromosphere in a binary potential and calculate the corresponding MT rate. We also implement our prescription in the stellar evolution code MESA. We show that chromospheric MT rates can be orders of magnitude higher than prior estimates for optically thin MT, especially for stars high on the red giant or asymptotic giant branch. This allows for substantial accretion before Roche lobe overflow, both for systems that undergo stable mass transfer and for systems that go through common envelope evolution. Thus, for a given initial binary configuration, this may alter the final period and component masses compared to those predicted classically. Our model is similar to Wind Roche-lobe Overflow, but it is physically rather than empirically motivated. We discuss implications for various post-interaction binaries that can be tested with population synthesis studies and observed binary populations. Additionally, we have identified an inaccuracy in the current implementation of the optically-thin Ritter 1988 prescription in MESA, which we correct.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is widely used in large-scale astrophysical simulations, but the resulting multilevel data are challenging to analyze quantitatively. We present simesh, an independent Python framework for quantitative analysis of cell-centered fields on block-structured AMR meshes. The current implementation targets three-dimensional Cartesian datasets from MPI-AMRVAC and compatible AGILE snapshots, preserving the native AMR hierarchy and connecting complementary scientific diagnostics within a common numerical representation. The framework combines Python workflow interfaces with compiled Cython kernels, supporting efficient analysis on AMR meshes. We compare native AMR analysis with a VTK point-data conversion and uniform-grid resampling, which shows that changes in data association, interpolation support, and differentiation scale affect both sampled magnetic fields and derived current densities. Small differences in the sampled primary field can become more pronounced in derivative-based quantities, particularly near coarse-fine interfaces. The applications combine field diagnostics, tracing, regional statistics, and line-of-sight integration on the same native AMR representation. simesh makes these operations available through reusable Python interfaces for reproducible analysis of multiscale simulation data.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We describe the propagation of a nonresonant light pulse normally incident on a thin dielectric slab using an integral-equation approach to electromagnetism. This emerges naturally from the microscopic picture of the material as made of polarizable atoms, confined within the material vacuum volume by their bonding interactions, each responding to the input radiation pulse as well as to the re-radiated pulses of the other atoms to which it is causally connected. The retarded integral equations are shown to be exactly equivalent to a local wave equation coupled to an auxiliary Lorentz-oscillator equation, which we solve numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme. For a slab thick enough that the front- and back-surface reflections are temporally separated, the front-surface reflectivity extracted from the simulation agrees with the Fresnel formula to within 1 percent, and the back-surface echo appears at exactly the expected round-trip delay. For a slab thinner than one optical cycle, the multiply-reflected wavelets overlap and interfere, and a full space-time map of the field directly visualizes the build-up of thin-film-like interference in the time domain. The material parameters used here are illustrative rather than fitted to measured data, and the numerical scheme is verified by an explicit grid-convergence study. In a companion paper (Paper II) the retarded integral equations are solved directly, without the local reformulation, and the two independent numerical solutions are shown to agree.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We present the first 3D lattice simulations of magnetic monopole production from a first-order phase transition, using the Press-Ryden-Spergel method, capturing the subsequent annihilation stage and the entry into the scaling regime in an expanding universe. We establish the quantitative relationship between the initial bubble number and the residual monopole abundance, and calculate the magnetic field and gravitational wave power spectra sourced by monopole dynamics. Crucially, we find that the magnetic field spectrum displays a steep $k^{-5}$ decline beyond the monopole size $w_M$, whereas the peak of the gravitational wave spectrum aligns with the scale of the mean monopole separation $d_M$, governed by $k^3$ and $k^{-3}$ scalings on the low- and high-wavenumber sides of the peak, respectively. However, since the resulting magnetic field strength is excluded by blazar observations, magnetic monopoles cannot be the origin of primordial cosmic magnetic fields. Finally, we determine the allowed monopole mass under the constraints of the Parker bound ($m_M\lesssim2.18\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) and dark matter abundance ($m_M\lesssim1.58\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$).

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below $T_\mathrm{F}\sim70$ K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of $\sim30-80$ K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature $T_\mathrm{p}\sim20-25$ K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr$_6$Sb$_6$ as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
EEG foundation models are advancing at an unprecedented pace, yet their evaluation is driven by downstream accuracy, which reveals little about whether their predictions rely on physiologically interpretable signal structure. We introduce a set of perturbation probes in two grounding axes: spatial grounding in channel identity and topographic locality, and spectral grounding in oscillatory content and waveform morphology. We apply these probes to five published EEG foundation models across motor-imagery and seizure recordings. Our experiments reveal differences in both representational sensitivity and downstream reliance. Electrode identity may be encoded without influencing downstream classification: permuting LaBraM's positional codes heavily displaced its embeddings yet reduced motor-imagery accuracy by only 1.2 points, while spectral details may be discriminable without producing specific responses to simulated clinical markers, as only REVE exceeded a spectral baseline on this task. These dissociations are hidden in common benchmarks, demonstrating how grounding probes can complement performance-based evaluation by revealing what EEG foundation models encode and what their predictions depend on.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Public descriptions of the Starlink downlink specify synchronization sequences, edge pilots, and predictable symbol templates, but leave the coded control fields and explicit payload-code representations largely unresolved. We examine one continuous complex-baseband capture spanning approximately 24 ms and recover control and coding structure beyond those predictable elements. Reference-phase removal exposes terminated rate-1/3 convolutional control blocks with constraint length seven and a group-level cyclic redundancy check. A conditional descriptor layout predicts sequential allocations through per-codeword symbol rounding, agreeing exactly with independently estimated endpoints in 16 of 18 frame records and within two symbols in the remaining records. Quasi-cyclic closure, binary elimination, and sparse dual checks yield explicit systematic code representations at rates 1/2 and 5/8. Frozen encoders predict 78,848, 9,984, and 811,008 reserved parity bits for three formats without disagreement. A rank-deficient long-code fit is completed within a declared finite structural family, and shared encoders are tested across modulation formats. The recovered representations explain observed coded symbols; they do not authenticate transmitter-standard identities or plaintext semantics. Two high-order formats have only one target field each, while codes 28 and 37 admit verified shortened cores with unexplained extra bits and code 4 remains unresolved.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Magneto-mechanical resonators (MMRs) are a recently introduced sensor technology for tracking and sensing applications that enables effective miniaturization down to the millimeter regime. However, estimating sensor parameters such as position from raw signals remains computationally challenging, because it requires solving a nonlinear inverse problem with computationally demanding objective function evaluations. In this work, we show how a deep learning method can accelerate this process by directly learning the inverse mapping from the measured signals. We consider the localization problem as an example and show that a convolutional-transformer regressor trained on simulated data with recorded noise can generalize to experimental data. The method achieves a median Euclidean distance error of 7 mm, which is comparable to the size of the sensor and corresponds to 6% of the size of a single coil. These results suggest that deep learning is a promising approach for rapid estimation of MMR parameters.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Thin film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising integrated photonic platform owing to its large quadratic nonlinearity enabling vital applications such as second-harmonic generation (SHG), optical parametric amplification, and spontaneous parametric down-conversion. However, to achieve high SH conversion efficiency, quasi-phase matching (QPM) through periodic electrical poling is typically required, which remains challenging in certain applications like multiple-ring coupled devices. Here, we demonstrate a surface molecule patterning strategy to enable QPM in a poling-free TFLN microring for SHG. An on-chip normalized conversion efficiency of approximately 11.5%/W is obtained in the poling-free TFLN microring with surface molecular pattern, showing an approximate 400-fold improvement compared to the same microring without surface molecular pattern. This approach offers a versatile route to engineer interfacial nonlinear interactions for nonlinear optics and quantum photonics applications and may be extended to multiple-ring coupled resonators and other platforms.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Optically addressable electron spin qubits that function at room temperature and under ambient conditions are essential for advancing quantum sensing. Solid state defect platforms offer robust spin-photon interfaces but lack precise defect positioning and electronic tunability. Molecular spin qubits enable bottom up chemical design yet suffer from limited photostability. Here, we introduce para-halophenyl (-Cl, -Br and -I) quantum defects in (6,5) single wall carbon nanotubes that trap triplet excitons with a spin-photon interface that is operable under ambient, room temperature conditions. These defects were shown to emit in the near infrared within the biological transparency window, and their placement on the nanotube surface provides nanoscale proximity to target environments. The deep optical traps formed by the defects yield exceptional photostability. Here, we demonstrate optical initialization and readout of these triplet states at room temperature, provide proof of principle sensing of paramagnetic molecules, and highlight potential for on chip detection. Together, these results establish SWCNT defects as a promising new platform for future quantum sensing.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe2. Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe2. We show that a chiral monoclinic (C2) structure is stabilized by the cooperative condensation of multiple phonon modes and reproduces the chiral topography and energy gap observed experimentally. We further find an exceptionally soft potential landscape around this energy-minimized structure, along the direction that removes the remaining rotational symmetry, allowing the lattice to fluctuate through fully asymmetric configurations while its average structure remains chiral. This dynamical chiral CDWnaturally reconciles the chiral domains seen by time-averaged topographic probes with the complete loss of symmetry detected by bulk spectroscopy, and clarifies how chiral CDWs emerge from the interplay of lattice instability and fluctuation.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Nanoscale nonreciprocal elements are needed to control signal flow in scalable quantum technologies, but existing nonreciprocal components are often bulky. Here, we show that a strongly nonreciprocal current-voltage relation can arise entirely from coherent elastic scattering in a mesoscopic Rashba nanowire with gate-defined scatterers. We first identify the symmetry constraints that enforce reciprocal transmission in a phase coherent conductor even when inversion and time-reversal symmetry are broken. We then show how gates that are capacitively coupled to the leads, together with a magnetic scatterer or transverse subband mixing, can remove these constraints. In the weak-scattering regime, nonreciprocal conductance originates from interference between distinct backscattering paths. In the strong-scattering regime, nonreciprocity can be resonantly enhanced by the hybridization of the transmitting channel with bound states that arise from a higher transverse subband or spin-split band. In this regime, we find that a bias-induced change in the gate potentials of about one percent can produce an order-unity diode response, i.e., electrons are transmitted almost as in a clean wire for one bias polarity, whereas for the other polarity the current is strongly suppressed.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Serendipity is important to design for, yet it remains difficult to measure and evaluate. No validated questionnaire exists, so studies either borrow ResQue's novelty scale, which does not measure serendipity, or build their own items, which makes findings hard to compare and synthesize. Building on our earlier conceptualization of experienced serendipity as a fortuitous encounter with content that is both refreshing and enriching, we developed the Serendiptionnaire, a questionnaire that operationalizes our framework. We conducted twenty-seven cognitive interviews over three iterations with respondents who varied in age, education level, country of birth, and English proficiency, while they browsed recommendations on platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Spotify. After each iteration, we revised the items until respondents interpreted them as intended. The resulting instrument consists of modular scales that researchers can combine to target the specific flavor of serendipity they want to study or design for. The Serendiptionnaire offers a ground truth for validating system-centered serendipity metrics and LLM-based evaluations, and it provides a nuanced evaluation of users' experienced serendipity.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In this paper, we prove the non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions $2\leq n\leq5$, resolving the corresponding low-dimensional case of a problem of Gromov. The proof combines the Jang deformation with capillary $μ$-bubble dimension reduction. We also establish weighted scalar--mean rigidity for Euclidean ball--torus products in total dimension at most seven and show that its hyperbolic analogue fails.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Blockchain consensus protocols implicitly follow a client-server architecture: validators are the only active participants, while clients (i.e., users) merely submit transactions and rely on validators to include them. This abstraction obscures a fundamental question: what should a client do to guarantee the timely inclusion of its own transaction? We study this question by introducing a leaderless consensus protocol in which clients are active. We define inclusion safety: the guarantee that a client's transaction enters some of the blocks produced for an epoch, and that every block omitting it belongs to a fork that is eventually abandoned. Because every transaction carries a reference to a block of the previous epoch, clients help select the surviving fork. This yields two paths to inclusion: reaching sufficiently many honest replicas within an epoch, or relaying a block containing the transaction across epochs until the corresponding fork becomes canonical. In a generalized model spanning synchrony and asynchrony, the client's and the replicas' connectivity are substitutes for inclusion safety: it is achieved either if the client is well connected, or if the client is poorly connected but honest replicas communicate reliably, provided the client reaches at least one of them. However, the substitution is imperfect: when inclusion safety rests on the replicas' connectivity, it requires a longer epoch compared to when the client is well connected.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Haptic teleoperation requires low-latency and reliable communication to preserve stable and responsive interaction between a human operator and a remote environment. However, network congestion can strongly degrade teleoperation performance, particularly when haptic traffic competes with other data flows for limited radio resources. This work investigates a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-assisted teleoperation framework over an Ericsson 5G standalone (SA) testbed under different congestion and quality-of-service (QoS) configurations. In the evaluated task, a human operator uses a haptic device to steer a spaceship through a remote virtual game. The DRL agent runs inside the remote environment, hosted at the network edge, and assists the operator by blending its own actions with the operator's commands received over the 5G network. This placement gives the agent direct access to the current state of the environment, unaffected by network delay. Experimental results show that DRL assistance improves task performance under all network conditions, with the largest benefit under congestion, where it reduces mean task completion time by 20.6%. Under congestion, assisted operation even outperforms unassisted operation with QoS prioritisation, which restores latency close to the uncongested baseline.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Retrieval-based in-context learning (ICL) enables large language models (LLMs) to predict tabular labels from similar examples, but it remains unclear whether LLM inference improves on direct voting over those same examples. We address this question by comparing four general-purpose LLMs with distance-weighted nearest-neighbor voting (Distance-KNN) using identical retrieved neighbors across 19 tabular classification datasets. With the number of demonstrations fixed, enlarging the retrieval candidate pool improves accuracy for all predictors, yet Distance-KNN achieves the highest mean accuracy at every pool size. More detailed analyses reveal that LLM gains are concentrated where retrieved neighbors exhibit low label consensus and vary across models. These gains further depend on the average feature-space distance to the test query: under low label consensus, some LLMs outperform Distance-KNN in close and intermediate neighborhoods, but all fall behind on average in the most distant group. Complementary experiments on the number of demonstrations, prompt formulation, retrieval representation, and label-balanced demonstration selection largely preserve the overall findings. These results characterize when LLM inference adds predictive value beyond distance-weighted voting in retrieval-based tabular ICL.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Multilingual patent prior-art retrieval requires identifying X-category references that are particularly relevant to the novelty or inventive step of a claimed invention, beyond topical similarity across languages and document views. We present X-Embedding, a two-stage framework that first learns patent-domain representations and then optimizes X-category retrieval relevance. The first stage aligns complementary sections within patents and corresponding sections across different-language patent-family members, learning from both patent structure and multilingual expressions. The second stage learns X-category relevance using examination-report X citations as positives and negatives drawn from retrieval candidates and A-category citations. Matryoshka representation learning (MRL) enables 64- and 1024-dimensional embeddings within one model. Evaluation on a common Chinese, English, and Japanese collection with four query views yields 89.09% overall macro Hit@100 at 64 dimensions, exceeding Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and RoBERTa by 21.25 and 3.68 percentage points, respectively. Under the same second-stage training and evaluation conditions, two-stage training outperforms direct supervised fine-tuning by 3.19 points, with gains of 5.34 and 4.72 points for English and Japanese and higher scores in nine of twelve language-view combinations. Overall macro Hit@10 and Hit@20 also improve by 3.71 and 3.79 points, respectively. These results support sequential patent-domain and task adaptation for improving aggregate X-category retrieval on this multilingual collection.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In this report, we introduce pplx-embed-v2-late, a pair of 0.6B and 9B multilingual and multimodal late-interaction models. Both models achieve state-of-the-art results within their respective size classes across a range of text, image, and visual document retrieval benchmarks. On visual document retrieval tasks, pplx-embed-v2-late-0.6b is competitive with models several times larger than itself. The models are trained via representation distillation from an 18B teacher. Consequently, they share an embedding space that supports asymmetric deployment: documents can be indexed with the 9B model and queried with the low-latency 0.6B model. Both models are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/perplexity-ai/pplx-embed-v2.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Multivariate scale-free texture images are nowadays central in numerous modern applications very different in nature. A common challenging issue consists of being able to generate such multivariate textures at any arbitrary size, from a learning set of (possibly much) smaller size. Parametric models often turn out to be too restrictive for the generation of realistic textures, thus prompting neural network training-based generation. While several neural network approaches propose generation at sizes larger than training, they do not explicitly assess the quality of the generation by quantifying how well multiscale or scale-free statistics in textures are reproduced and rather rely on perceptual assessment. The present work combines convolutional Wasserstein-GAN architectures with self-attention layers to generate textures of arbitrary size while focusing on reproducing multiscale statistics, without coding a model into the loss function. The relevance of using a self-attention layer is studied. Quantitative assessment conducted on multifractal textures, representative of a broad class of multiscale textures, over ten independent trainings shows that the proposed architecture is able to generate textures with accurate statistics for sizes $8 \times 8$ larger than the originals. The results show that placing self-attention in the critic provides the most consistent performance across output sizes.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Request migration and interruption recovery in distributed large language model (LLM) inference rely on historical key-value (KV) caches. Retaining or transferring a complete cache incurs substantial state overhead, whereas replaying historical tokens requires additional computation. This paper proposes RISK-KV, a quality-aware method for selective historical KV reconstruction in pretrained models. RISK-KV uses exact KV states on both sides of a target layer and cross-layer ridge regression to predict the missing layer's attention-projection input; it then folds in the original model's KV projection matrices to reduce predictor storage. Reconstruction risk is measured by the change in negative log-likelihood (NLL) caused by actual reconstruction, and low-overhead topology search with quality gating selects the layer groups to reconstruct. Independent tests on three language models show that representative recovery configurations omit 18.2 percent to 33.3 percent of historical KV, with perplexity changes below 0.5 percent. In a local request-recovery experiment with a 512-token history, RISK-KV achieves a 1.51 to 3.31 times speedup over full Token Replay. These results indicate that selective KV reconstruction can reduce historical cache overhead with small changes in predictive quality and improve request-recovery efficiency under the evaluated deployment conditions.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In particle communication, particles released for different symbols can reach the receiver at overlapping times, making reliable detection difficult. This paper develops a digital communication framework that connects particle transport, pulse shaping, and receiver processing for three-dimensional free-space diffusion-advection channels. We derive the continuous-time and discrete-time frequency responses and explain how flow speed affects channel delay and bandwidth. Under advection-dominated conditions, the group delay approaches $R/V$, and the one-sided $3$-dB bandwidth scales as $V^{3/2}$. We design nonnegative, unit-energy transmit pulses using a packet-level SINR criterion that includes interference from both preceding and subsequent symbols under additive white Gaussian receiver noise. Simulations validate the analytical approximations and show that optimized pulses spread across more of the symbol interval when noise is substantial and become narrower as noise decreases. BER evaluations across SNR and symbol duration compare optimized, rectangular, and single-impulse pulses with several detection methods, identifying the operating conditions in which transmit-pulse design improves reliability.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In STOC 1972, J{ü}rg Nievergelt and Edward M.~Reingold introduced the $BB[α]$-tree, also known as a \emph{weight-balanced} tree, which for any $α\in (0,\frac{1}{2}]$ is a binary search tree where every node with induced subtree size $s$ has children with induced subtree sizes at least $α(s+1)-1$. A new rotation-based binary search tree, the \emph{PopTree}, is introduced. The PopTree stores $n$ elements and is a $BB[\tfrac1{20}]$-tree after the execution of each search and a $BB[\tfrac1{729}]$-tree at all times, notably while rebalancing. For any constant $α$, its performance on search sequences of length $Ω(n \log n)$ is proved to be within a constant factor (which can depend on $α$) of the optimal offline rotation-based binary search tree that maintains the $BB[α]$ balance invariant.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study the cosmology of self-interacting ultralight dark matter. The scalar field evolves from an early Hubble-frozen phase to a quartic-dominated radiation-like phase and finally to a quadratic matter-like phase. The intermediate phase increases the pre-recombination expansion rate and reduces the sound horizon, while the late phase allows the same field to contribute to dark matter. We implement the background and linear perturbations of a mixed cold-dark-matter and ultralight-dark-matter cosmology in CLASS. For $m=10^{-22}\,{\rm eV}$ and $\tilde m\simeq1\,{\rm eV}$, increasing the ultralight-dark-matter fraction raises the fixed-$θ_*$ value of $H_0$, lowers the late-time clustering amplitude, strengthens the scale-dependent matter-power suppression, and produces a smooth CMB-temperature residual reaching about $9\%$ for the largest fraction considered. The model therefore generates simultaneous background and growth shifts in the directions relevant to the Hubble and structure-growth tensions. Establishing whether these shifts improve a joint fit requires a likelihood-level observational analysis.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We use the monopole and quadrupole power spectra of [\ion{O}{2}]-emitting galaxies in the HETDEX Public Data Release 1 to constrain the growth of cosmic structures at $z\le0.48$. We interpret the power spectra using a simulation-based model built from the Mucho-Uchuu-1G $N$-body simulation. The best-fit model reproduces the observed power spectra remarkably well up to $k_\mathrm{max}=0.7~h~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$, and goodness-of-fit tests confirm that the HETDEX [\ion{O}{2}] clustering is consistent with the \textit{Planck} flat $Λ$CDM cosmology. We test the general relativity (GR) prediction for the linear growth index, $γ\simeq 0.55$. When the Alcock-Paczyński parameters are held fixed at their fiducial values, we find consistency with the GR prediction, $γ=0.55\pm 0.05$. And, when the AP parameters are allowed to vary, $γ=0.60\pm 0.07$, which is consistent with both the GR prediction and the suppressed growth rate reported by \citet{Nguyen_2023}. These results establish HETDEX [\ion{O}{2}] galaxies as a competitive, independent low-redshift probe of the growth of structures and motivate future full cosmological inference.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g \le 2n(n-1)ω_n \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. Here $ω_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball and $v=V_{M^n}$ is the asymptotic volume ratio. In dimension three, with the center at a pole, we obtain a sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le16πr, \] without any positive volume growth assumption. We also obtain a bound for every asymptotic volume ratio which is sharp for $0\le v\le1/4$. Under nonnegative sectional curvature and $v>0$, we prove the explicit bound at arbitrary centers \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le12π(1-v)v^{-3}r. \] If $0\le1-v\le1/100$, we further obtain \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le\bigl[8π(1-v)+200π(1-v)^2\bigr]r. \] The leading coefficient $8π$ is sharp, and a remainder of quadratic order in $1-v$ is necessary.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Edge medical segmentation must reconcile small model size, high accuracy, and fast inference. TernScope addresses this tradeoff through model--hardware co-design, learning a compact segmentation network whose low-bit operators also simplify hardware execution. Split-channel large-kernel blocks preserve spatial context with limited computation, while branch fusion removes redundant inference paths. Ternary Progressive Quantization-aware Training (TPQ) then adapts the fused network from deep to shallow layers, through the decoder, and finally to the input and prediction layers. All 25 convolutions use ternary weights and 8-bit activations, enabling packed storage and multiplier-free computation. The resulting model uses 0.2483 M parameters and 0.0949 GMACs while retaining competitive segmentation accuracy on in-domain and external datasets. Under the same 45 nm technology, TernScope reduces compute-array area by 88.46% compared with the original Gemmini, a systolic-array accelerator with 8-bit $\times$ 8-bit multipliers. These results demonstrate a path from accurate lightweight medical segmentation to compact low-bit hardware.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The transition metal oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ exhibits a non-collinear spin-ice like antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N \approx $ 90 K due to complex magnetic exchange interactions and axial single-ion anisotropy of Fe$^{2+}$ spins. The magnetic structure was deduced/determined from combined $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and $^{139}$La-NMR on polycrystalline specimen. In this work, we present zero-field $^{139}$La-NQR investigations on polycrystalline La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ in a broad frequency and temperature range between 2.8 - 20 MHz and 4.2 - 100 K. The measured resonances at $ν_Q$, $2 \, ν_Q$, and $3 \, ν_Q$ are fully consistent with the previous NMR studies and also with the magnetic structure. A substantial modification of the electric field gradient at the La-position below $T_N$ is inconsistent with the current investigations.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Wave computing offers a compelling route to bypass the latency and energy bottlenecks of digital baseband processing. However, existing wave-domain processors rely on task-specific, non-convex iterative optimization, which incurs substantial configuration overhead and limits real-time applications. In this paper, we propose the wave processing unit (WPU), a programmable planar Mach--Zehnder interferometer (MZI) network that accelerates matrix--vector multiplications in MIMO communications. First, we model the tunable MZI element as a parameterized $2\times2$ unitary transformation, and establish a closed-form synthesis framework for the WPU that decomposes an arbitrary unitary matrix into a cascade of MZI elements arranged in a compact rectangular topology. To handle arbitrary complex-valued operators, we further extend the method through singular value decomposition (SVD) and a hardware-efficient semi-unitary synthesis, avoiding redundant hardware and reducing the compilation complexity. We then apply the WPU to multiuser downlink precoding by an efficient WPU synthesis method, and compare the proposed architecture with hybrid and wave-domain ones. Numerical results demonstrate machine-precision synthesis with negligible residuals for up to $64\times64$ operators, with approximately $380\times$ faster configuration than iterative wave computing baselines. For 64-antenna, 8-user downlink precoding, WPU requires 87.5% fewer RF chains than the fully digital architecture while achieving the same sum rate under ideal hardware. These results highlight the potential of the WPU for precise, hardware-efficient wave-domain processing with rapid configuration.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Combining topological insulators with chiral magnetic multilayers offers the opportunity to greatly enhance the spin-orbit torque (SOT) driven manipulation of hosted spin textures, however this also exposes devices to the often poor temperature stability of the commonly used, Bi$_2$X$_3$-based (X is a chalcogenic element), topological insulator films. In this work we demonstrate through in-situ-annealing and polarised neutron reflectometry that the multilayer at a Bi$_2$Se$_3$ interface remains magnetically robust up to a temperature of 350 $^{\circ}$C: even as the Bi$_2$Se$_3$ epilayer structurally deteriorates. Through x-ray photoemission electron microscopy, an intermediate annealing temperature of $\sim$ 200 $^{\circ}$C was found to improve the domain ordering of the multilayer, allowing for field-induced skyrmion nucleation, all whilst sustaining minimal damage to the topological insulator

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Nitrogen-rich (N-rich) field stars (likely second-generation escapees from globular clusters) provide a powerful, but currently sample-limited, probe of globular-cluster disruption in the Galactic halo. We exploit the fact that enhanced NH, CN absorption depresses optical u band flux, while the near-ultraviolet (NUV) band is largely insensitive to nitrogen enhancement while remaining sensitive to overall metallicity. Combining GALEX NUV photometry with (synthetic) SDSS optical photometry, we construct a [Fe/H]-dependent stellar-locus model for giants and select significant redder u-g outliers as N-rich candidates. For a relaxed cut ([Fe/H] <= -0.8, 2 sigma) we identify 970 candidates, with an estimated completeness of 64-65% and purity of 41-62% from multiple validations. A stricter selection ([Fe/H] <= -1.0, 3 sigma) yields 220 candidates, with lower completeness (30-38%) but substantially higher purity (60-91%). The dominant contaminants show anomalous spectral energy distributions (e.g., UV excess), and are themselves useful targets for follow-up. The diverse kinematic and dynamical properties of our candidates suggest multiple origins. This scalable photometric approach enables systematic searches for N-rich halo stars and is well suited to forthcoming wide-field surveys such as CSST.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Kagome lattices host rich magnetic, topological, and transport phenomena owing to their geometric frustration and strong spin correlations. Here we present a systematic neutron scattering study of the kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$, which orders into a collinear $c$-axis antiferromagnetic (AF) state below $T_N =$ 551 K. An additional anomalous Hall effect (AHE) contribution beyond the conventional magnetization-scaling response is observed well below $T_N$ under an in-plane magnetic field $\mathbf{B} \parallel ab$. Elastic neutron scattering demonstrates that the Fe moments preserve their collinear $c$-axis AF alignment down to 1.5 K at zero field. Inelastic neutron scattering reveals a distinctive Y-shape spin excitation dispersion exhibiting a two-gap structure below 10 meV, likely arising from two nondegenerate spin-wave branches. Polarized neutron measurements further show that the low-temperature spin excitations are strongly anisotropic: the in-plane component $M_{ab}$ dominates while the $c$-axis component $M_c$ is nearly absent. Upon warming, $M_c$ gradually grows markedly but remains much weaker than $M_{ab}$ even at 300 K. We propose that the unconventional AHE originates from a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting either in the static or dynamic configurations due to gapless excitations. These findings establish the collinear AF kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$ as a platform for chirality-driven AHE without spontaneous spin reorientation.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The nucleon is the multiplicative counterpart of the nucleolus: it lexicographically maximizes the fraction of its stand-alone value that each coalition receives. We study exact nucleon computation in matching games and in two extensions: $b$-matching games, in which players may have several partners, and partitioned matching games, in which one player may own several vertices. We resolve three open problems from a recent survey. For ordinary matching games with nonnegative rational weights, we give a polynomial-time combinatorial algorithm using maximum-weight matching, shortest paths, and minimum-cost flow, ; it returns both a nucleon allocation and a compact description of the full nucleon. In contrast, computing any nucleon allocation is NP-hard for unit-weight $b$-matching games with capacities at most three and for unit-weight partitioned matching games of width at most three. Finally, for the unresolved capacity-two case, we show that exact nucleon computation is polynomial-time Turing reducible to SHORTEST NON-ZERO CYCLE.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
After the beginning of photography of solar corona during the eclipses in the year 1860, efforts began to carry out spectroscopic observations of solar corona. During the total solar eclipse of 1868 August 18 at Guntur, Madras state, the observation of emission line 5875Å by Janssen lead to the discovery of Helium. Next year, during the eclipse of 1869 August 7, Charles Young and William Harkness discovered green emission line around 5310Å (later measured as 5303Å). It was interpreted as due to Coronium, an unknown element. The identification of this green line in 1939 due to [Fe xiv] ion showed the corona to be hot at 10^6 K. High resolution spectroscopic observations indicated that width of emission lines to be more than expected. The excess line width was interpreted in terms of existence of non-thermal velocity. Recent spectroscopic observations have indicated a complex nature of variation of emission line parameters with height above the corona. The spectroscopy of solar corona is also performed in other wavelengths, such as UV, EUV, X-rays, visible, infrared, and radio part of the spectrum. Here, we discuss the past spectroscopic observations of solar corona, present observations with various instruments, such as Visible Emission Line Coronagraph onboard Aditya-L1, and need for the spectroscopic observations in future.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In high-mobility channels, the widely adopted orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation waveform suffers from significant performance degradation due to channel variation and severe inter-carrier interference. Although delay-Doppler (DD) domain multicarrier (DDMC) modulation enjoys a higher channel estimation (CE) accuracy via exploiting the inherent DD-domain channel stability, sparsity, and separability, its high detection complexity limits its practical deployment, making OFDM still a promising waveform candidate for the sixth-generation (6G) cellular networks. To simultaneously harness the complementary strengths of DDMC and OFDM and mitigate their respective limitations, this paper proposes a DD-domain aided OFDM (DD-a-OFDM) framework, including a pulsone pilot (PP) design and a cross-domain iterative receiver design, to enhance the CE and detection performance of OFDM in high-mobility channels. Specifically, a pulsone pilot sequence is periodically inserted before the cyclic prefix (CP) for each OFDM symbol in the time-domain, which is equivalent to a single DD-domain pilot impulse and enables accurate DD-domain CE. Then, we propose a cross-domain iterative receiver in which the time-frequency (TF) domain detection results are transformed into the DD-domain for interference cancellation and CE; in turn, the DD-domain estimated channel is transformed into the TF-domain for channel reconstruction and symbol detection. The proposed cross-domain iterative receiver achieves a higher CE accuracy and detection performance with a much lower pilot overhead, compared to the conventional OFDM system. Simulation results validate the fast convergence and superior performance of the proposed DD-a-OFDM scheme and demonstrate that it maintains a robust CE and detection performance even in high-mobility channels.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Nematic fluctuations alter the low-energy electronic behavior and reshape the mean-field phase diagram. We study a two-dimensional nematic metal with a two-component internal degree of freedom. Near the quantum critical point (QCP), longitudinal nematic fluctuations generate the non-Fermi-liquid self-energy $\propto|ω|^{2/3}$, whereas transverse fluctuations give a subleading logarithmic, marginal-Fermi-liquid correction. Nevertheless, the transverse sector dominates the correction to the phase diagram through a quantum order-by-disorder mechanism: the emergent nematic background reshapes the electronic spectrum, alters the decay of nematic bosons, and produces a negative singular free-energy correction. This correction reconstructs the phase diagram, drives the transition first order, and is described by a scaling function whose two asymptotic limits define two critical regimes with free-energy corrections scaling as $R^{8/3}$ and $R^3$, respectively, where $R$ is the order-parameter magnitude; their powers follow from the competition between the characteristic momentum of normal-state nematic fluctuations and that of the ordered-state background. These two regimes are experimentally distinguishable through nematic-susceptibility hysteresis measurements. The corrected phase diagram shows that the enlarged nodal $α$ phase masks the otherwise bare QCP, making it inaccessible; consequently, the logarithmic self-energy correction is by no means negligible at low energies.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Improving the temporal and spatial resolution of spectroscopy inevitably reduces the photons available to each measurement, pushing rapid measurements into photon-starved conditions where weak spectral features are obscured by stochastic background noise. Here, we present Fast2Peak (F2P), a self-supervised Transformer framework that transforms the spectral restoration task into a context-prediction problem. Given that physically constrained spectral signals exhibit strong local continuity, whereas the stochastic noise fluctuates randomly and does not possess the continuity across neighboring spectral pixels, single-pixel masking enables F2P to restore the predictable signal structure while suppressing unpredictable fluctuations even without clean reference spectra. Unlike conventional offline spectral restoration, F2P achieves high-fidelity restoration within milliseconds, enabling real-time "acquire-and-process" operation. We demonstrate this capability in time-resolved electrochemical SERS and hyperspectral Raman imaging, where spectral restoration is performed during data acquisition. In addition, F2P has demonstrated its robust generalization across different instruments and spectral modalities, including Raman, NMR, XRD and FTIR.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The recent measurement of baryon acoustic oscillations by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument reveals a mild tension with observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) within the standard $Λ$CDM cosmological model. Another interesting hint beyond standard cosmology arises from recent analyses of Planck polarization data which has been interpreted as cosmic birefringence. One possible solution to explain both observations is to introduce cosmic birefringence induced by axion-like particles (ALPs) that has a much larger rotation angle during the reionization epoch than that during the recombination: the large rotation suppresses the $EE$ reionization signal, allowing an elevated value of the CMB optical depth $τ$ that alleviates the CMB-BAO tension. In this paper, we explore a scenario where the energy transfers from matter to ALPs before the reionization. Using Planck low-$\ell$ $EE$, $BB$, and $EB$ data, we show that, for energy injection at $10 \lesssim z \lesssim 100$, there exist parameter regions where $τ\simeq 0.08-0.10$ is compatible with the data.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Applying standard Bayesian methods to the most reliably known unclassified facts about the Covid epidemic allows crude estimation of the odds for research-related vs. purely zoonotic origins. Here a broadly inclusive zoonotic hypothesis is compared with a rather specific subset of the research-related hypothesis defined by known prior work and grant proposals. The important observations are the type of virus, the city of the first outbreak, the lack of known prior hosts, the anomalous early pattern of evolution, and two specific features of the viral sequence. The resulting odds strongly favor research. The odds remain fairly strong under inclusion of uncertainties in prior odds.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $π:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. FDTD also reveals a transition from multi-mode to single-longitudinal-mode behavior in 200-nm fins, consistent with experimentally observed fringe narrowing. Increasing fin length from 10 μm to 30 μm compresses fringe spacing via longer round-trip paths. Conversely, tilting the fin end-facet from 90° to 45° reduces the effective light path length, increasing the incoherent optical emission. Remarkably, this loss can be offset by adjusting the fin length-to-height ratio. Results suggest WARCL is a robust in-situ method for direct characterization of individual dielectric nanocavities, mapping their modal profiles and light directionality as a function of geometry for custom design of nanoscale optical sources and waveguides.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2π$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Long contexts increase the memory cost of the key-value (KV) cache in large language model (LLM) inference. Sparse attention reduces attention computation and memory traffic by selecting historical tokens, but the retained KV cache must remain available for later decoding steps. We present UlaCache, a KV cache management system built around a unified logical address space spanning GPU KV pools and optional CPU memory. Stable logical references let the inference engine allocate and select KV independently of physical placement. Common allocation and sparse-access interfaces support data-parallel (DP) and tensor-parallel (TP) attention. For distributed storage, local GPU buffers retain selected KV across decoding steps, so only missing entries require transfers. When CPU storage is enabled, Parallel Bucketed LRU (PB-LRU) manages a GPU pool shared across requests. It updates recency metadata and selects eviction victims in parallel. UlaCache transfers KV and then updates the address mappings. With speculative decoding enabled under matched CPU and GPU memory budgets, UlaCache achieves peak decoding throughput speedups of 1.16 $\times$ (DP) and 1.70 $\times$ (TP) on H200, and 1.73 $\times$ (DP) and 2.51 $\times$ (TP) on B300, compared with the state-of-the-art baseline.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The mid-wave infrared (MWIR, 3-5 microns) is indispensable for thermal sensing, gas detection, long-range imaging, and free-space optical communications. Meta-optics offer a compact, lightweight, and potentially low-cost alternative to conventional refractive optics, making them attractive for size, weight, and power (SWaP)-constrained systems. However, their strong chromatic dispersion has largely restricted imaging to narrow spectral bands. Here, we demonstrate broadband imaging across the full 3-5 micron MWIR band using a single-layer silicon metasurface coupled with computational reconstruction. Remarkably, the reconstruction model is adapted using only four image captures, overcoming large training data requirements and enabling broadband image recovery despite the strongly wavelength-dependent optical response. In contrast to approaches that engineer complex, dispersion-optimized metalens profiles for broadband operation, our method leverages the wavelength-dependent information encoded by a simple 2cm diameter hyperboloid metalens. We show that this metasurface captures sufficient broadband intensity information for computational reconstruction across the entire MWIR band. These results establish a simple route toward broadband computational meta-optics without requiring broadband achromatic metalens designs, offering a promising platform for compact MWIR imaging systems.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.
