Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Age assurance faces a fundamental privacy dilemma: meaningful assurance typically requires revealing identity or other sensitive information, whereas privacy-preserving alternatives often provide little assurance. Existing approaches either disclose sensitive information directly or shift the disclosure and trust requirement to an identity provider, while self-declared age provides little meaningful assurance. Thus, a fundamental gap remains between establishing an age property and revealing information beyond what is necessary to establish that property. We present \textit{A-GE} (Age-Grounded Evidence), a privacy-preserving age assurance system that derives age-related evidence from fine-grained motion captured by commodity inertial measurement units (IMUs). A-GE exploits subtle motion dynamics that we hypothesize reflect underlying neuromuscular and physiological processes during ordinary device interaction. It requires neither identity information nor government identification and operates across available sensor sampling rates, including the approximately 60~Hz limit of web-based sensing, with configurable minimum-age thresholds ranging from 14 to 21 years. We evaluate A-GE on more than 600 participants, with separate participant-disjoint cohorts for model development and final evaluation. At a 16-year minimum-age threshold, A-GE achieves up to 93.8\% accuracy with a comparable F1 score across the evaluated configurations. We further demonstrate client-side deployment on Android, iOS, and the web, and examine unintended attribute inference and residual privacy risks, characterizing both the privacy benefits and limitations of deriving age evidence from commodity motion.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed. The result rests on a deterministic identity: for arbitrary vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the number of orderings for which the convex hull of the partial sums avoids the origin equals the number of permutations for which the convex hull of the cycle sums avoids it. We derive it from a permutation-averaging identity for valuations obtained in our earlier work. Consequences include the identities of Sparre Andersen and Spitzer, the distribution-free absorption probabilities of Kabluchko, Vysotsky and Zaporozhets, their generating function found by Petrov, Randon-Furling and Zaporozhets, and a formula for the probability that the origin is never absorbed.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In the age of AI, privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search over high-dimensional embeddings has emerged as a critical yet frustratingly challenging domain, dominated by tradeoffs between speed, privacy, and accuracy. Traditional tree and graph-based indexing structures (e.g., HNSW, ScaNN) rely fundamentally on non-linear operations that are computationally intractable under Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) or blind server-side constraints. In this paper, we introduce Holo-NN (Holographic Nearest Neighbor Search), an algebraic framework that replaces data-dependent branching with a single linear projection. Our key observation is that while distances across a database are dense, neighborhood membership is inherently sparse: only a handful of points ever lie close to a query. By pairing locality-preserving feature transforms with Compressive Sensing, Holo-NN folds the entire database offline into a compact holographic sensing matrix. At query time, encrypted search reduces to a single, non-interactive matrix-vector multiplication---requiring no FHE bootstrapping, no multi-round interaction, and no client-side index state. This turns private retrieval into an embarrassingly parallel, accuracy-tunable computation that runs out of the box on both CPUs and GPUs, scaling efficiently to production databases. We offer a comparison against other state-of-the-art Private ANN algorithms to help situate the method in the broader context of production-grade private retrieval.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In this paper, we introduce braided cuckoo hashing, an open-addressed hash table that supports load factor up to $1 - \varepsilon$ (for some parameter $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$), while supporting queries, insertions, and deletions in worst-case time $O(\log \varepsilon^{-1})$, with high probability. This result represents an exponential improvement on insertion/deletion time over previous constructions, and disproves a conjecture of Bender, Kuszmaul, and Zhou that the product of worst-case query time and expected insertion/deletion time must be $Ω(\varepsilon^{-1})$.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study optimal intervention design problems aimed at minimizing the aggregate volatility in network systems. We consider linear network equilibrium models arising in network games, production networks, and opinion dynamics, where exogenous shocks hitting a few nodes can propagate through the network and cause detrimental systemic effects. Focusing on idiosyncratic shocks, we first identify a general network centrality measure that determines the amplification factor of the variance of each node's shock to the aggregate system volatility, and show that, in relevant special cases, it reduces to Katz-Bonacich, cycle, and concentration centralities. We then consider a system planner who can attenuate the shocks on the nodes, subject to a budget constraint, so as to minimize the aggregate volatility. We solve this problem analytically and show that its solution has a water-filling-type structure: for low budget, the intervention is concentrated on the node(s) maximizing a quantity ω_i that combines the shock's variance, the node's centrality, and the intervention cost; as the budget increases, more and more nodes are targeted, and for sufficiently large budget every node with ω_i > 0 receives an intervention proportional to ω_i. Finally, we study a robust version of the problem, where the planner minimizes the volatility against the worst-case vector of shock variances chosen by an adversary within a given budget. We solve this min-max problem analytically and show that its solution also has a water-filling-type structure, with the ratio between the node's centrality and the square root of the adversarial cost playing the role of ω_i.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Cybersecurity operators increasingly encounter sophisticated and fast-paced attacks, making autonomous cyber defense (ACD) a critical approach for supporting timely and effective decision-making. Reinforcement learning (RL)-based ACD agents have the ability to autonomously observe network states and take actions to defend and recover system assets, making them well suited for ACD. However, these agents often face critical trade-offs, such as improving network security while inadvertently degrading service availability or violating other operational priorities such as confidentiality and integrity, raising the core challenge of aligning agent behavior with human-specified goals and intent. In this work, we study the problem of aligning RL-based ACD agents with human-specified operational objectives without requiring costly retraining. We formalize alignment for ACD as a policy shaping problem, where a pretrained RL decision-making policy can be adjusted at test time using predicted attributes over agent actions. We also propose an adaptive approach that dynamically controls the alignment--performance trade-off as operational priorities shift during an ongoing cyber attack. We evaluate our method in a simulated cyber defense environment, CybORG, analyzing performance across multiple alignment objectives using the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) information security triad. Our results show that adaptive test-time policy shaping can significantly improve alignment while preserving core cyber defense performance, offering a practical and scalable alternative to training-time alignment methods in RL. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/ITM-Kitware/alignment-cage-challenge-2.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The Tulczyjew-Dixon centroid of a massive spinning particle, built as a composite of canonical Poincaré variables, carries the exact coordinate algebra $\{X^μ,X^ν\}=-S^{μν}/p^2$, whose noncommutativity bivector is the transverse spin tensor of the particle itself rather than an external background. That bracket and its Compton-scale magnitude are already known, and we recover them here as the starting point of the analysis, not as a result. What the composite realization settles is the domain on which the algebra may be used. Closure of the Jacobi identity requires $p^{-2}$ to remain operator valued, and the exactness domain is the convex timelike interior $Ω_μ$, on which states supported on a single mass shell are distributional. We show that freezing $p^2$ to its shell value inside the centroid leaves every two-operator commutator unchanged on shell, so that the projected position dictionary, the Berry cancellation and the endpoint transversality identity are untouched, while the same substitution fails from three insertions onward, with residue the truncated Jacobiator $2ε^{μνρσ}W_σ/(p^2)^2$. This two-versus-three criterion replaces the qualitative restriction to shell-preserving matrix elements and states which constructions built on a fixed-shell bivector $Θ_m$ remain valid. We then follow the algebra through positive-energy projection, packet-conditioned Moyal fibers, Compton routing holonomy and projected nonassociative products, recording for each layer whether it falls on the safe side of the criterion. No prediction beyond QED follows. In the geometric branch the physical amplitude reduces to the QED amplitude, and the transverse matching coefficients remain uncomputed.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Assessing compound risks requires a model for routine and extreme joint behaviour together, and a principled answer to where the joint tail begins. We propose the self-thresholding angular-radial (STAR) model: after marginal standardization, the radius given the angle follows a spliced distribution, with a flexible body below an angle-dependent threshold curve and a generalized Pareto tail above it. The threshold curve is estimated with all other parameters, so its uncertainty propagates to every summary, and the joint density is in closed form because the splice normalizes in one dimension for every angle. The tail scale function is the reciprocal gauge of the implied limit set, and the coefficient of extremal association is an explicit parameter, so a prior with atoms at tail independence and at the asymptotic dependence boundary yields posterior probabilities of the dependence class. At that boundary the copula of the model is asymptotically dependent, while its margins and joint tail are both lighter than exponential by a factor inversely proportional to the level. Simulations show accurate recovery of finite-level dependence summaries within and beyond the model class, and the slow separation of asymptotic dependence from strong asymptotic independence that the theory predicts. For warm-season daily maxima of fine particulate matter and ozone at a Beijing station, the pair is asymptotically independent with posterior probability 0.96 and both pollutants exceed their 0.9 quantiles on about two and a half days per season; the model gives summaries comparable to those of existing approaches without requiring the arbitrary choice of a threshold. The construction extends to d dimensions through pairwise deficits of the gauge, illustrated by adding coarse particulate matter as a third pollutant.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
A multi-step induction-assisted hot rotary swaging route was developed for the novel dual-phase Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy to investigate the evolution of microstructure, crystallographic texture, and mechanical properties during sequential deformation. Phase-transformation temperatures determined by electrical resistivity measurements were used to select processing conditions in the single-phase $β$ field at 880°C and the $α+β$ field at 780°C. Induction heating with thermographic temperature control enabled reduction of the initial 12 mm rod to 6.3 mm, corresponding to a total area reduction of 72%. Swaging in the $β$ field refined millimetre-sized prior-$β$ grains to approximately 100 $μ$m, while subsequent cooling produced a fine lamellar $α+β$ microstructure. Further deformation in the $α+β$ field disrupted the lamellar structure, promoted globularisation and recrystallisation of the $α$ phase, and refined the $β$ phase. The microstructural evolution was accompanied by a pronounced $\langle 11\bar{2}0\rangle_α\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ fibre texture in the $α$ phase, whereas the $β$ phase exhibited predominantly $\langle 110\rangle_β\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ together with a $\langle 111\rangle_β\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ component. The phase constitution remained comparatively stable, with approximately 12-15 wt.% retained $β$ throughout processing. Subsequent $α+β$ swaging decreased the compressive yield strength from 1103 to 839 MPa while increasing plastic deformability, with a maximum fracture strain of 32%. Radial hardness heterogeneity was progressively eliminated. These results demonstrate that induction-assisted rotary swaging in selected phase fields provides an effective route for tailoring microstructure, texture, and mechanical response in dual-phase zirconium alloys.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Odd-parity spin splitting constrains magnetic band crossings but does not determine their topological descendants. We show that the Chern contribution of an isolated inverted sector is controlled by the phase winding of its transverse mass pair: when the masses and tangential velocities reverse together, contributions from successive Dirac points add rather than cancel. This distinguishes topological winding from the polynomial degree labeling the magnetic parent. For specified complementary masses, periodic tetragonal $h$- and hexagonal $j$-wave models host eight and twelve same-chirality Weyl points on a momentum plane, with gapped-slice Chern numbers $|C|=4$ and $6$, respectively. A microscopic four-band $p$-wave model identifies an antiunitary obstruction to first-order transverse masses and demonstrates a symmetry-broken $C=1$ phase at quarter filling. First-principles calculations for the proposed coplanar spin-vortex texture of LaMnAu$_5$ reveal the $h$-wave nodal pattern, its anisotropic spin--orbit reconstruction, and a mirror-channel spectral response that reverses under opposite spin rotations. Together, these results distinguish the symmetry of an odd-parity magnetic parent from the mass structure controlling the topology of its descendants.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Regulated industries such as finance and healthcare face critical governance challenges that hamper the adoption of AI-assisted software development and hinder the transition from experimental pilots to production work. This paper presents Zafin AIOS, an end-to-end orchestration platform and control plane designed to deploy AI within regulated industries such as finance. We provide the architectural principles and an empirical comparison between AI-assisted and human-led workloads. To validate this framework empirically, we conduct a case study analysis of Zafin's internal enterprise workflows, which we refer to as Customer Zero. This paper contributes a production case study of AI-assisted software engineering in regulated industries. We evaluate the results of using Zafin AIOS with two different production codebases, one for the pricing execution platform and the other for the client deal negotiation platform. Our contribution is a customer case study for regulated industries with production codebases and governance, which includes proof of work. The results demonstrate that strictly governed agentic orchestration increases enterprise capacity without compromising control. In the pricing execution platform workflows, the platform provided complete observability and reduced effort by 38\%. In the client deal negotiation platform, it reduced reporting work by 76\% while maintaining all predefined data privacy, role-based access, and audit guardrails. This paper bridges the gap between AI-assisted software engineering theory and the operational reality of compliance. Closing this gap is important to help enterprises take advantage of AI technologies. These results are descriptive of the benefits of using governed workflows in regulated industries.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Policy decisions often depend on whether the average treatment effect (ATE) exceeds a specific cutoff. In instrumental variable (IV) settings, point identification of the ATE requires strong assumptions that are often difficult to justify. Therefore, many researchers shift their attention to identification of the local (L) ATE or target bounds of the ATE. Both strategies have well-known drawbacks: the substantive relevance of the LATE is frequently questioned, and the bounds are often too wide to be informative. We propose a simple sensitivity analysis that allows researchers to maintain focus on the ATE, and then discuss its connection to related bounding procedures. Based on these results, researchers can decide, in a principled manner, whether the sign of the ATE is inferable under assumptions they deem credible. The proposed strategies are easy to apply, and we illustrate their value with two real-data examples. The R package ivate implements our procedures.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We consider elastic vector meson production in longitudinally polarized electron-proton collisions at small $x$. Inspired by previous pioneering proposals in the literature, we calculate the numerator of the longitudinal double-spin asymmetry (DSA) within the polarized small-$x$ formalism for both the transversely and longitudinally polarized vector mesons. Our calculation demonstrates that the $\cosφ_{kΔ}$ azimuthal harmonic of the DSA for the elastic vector meson production at small transverse momentum transfer (with $φ_{kΔ}$ the azimuthal angle between the transverse momenta of the outgoing electron and meson in the dipole/Trento frame) provides a promising probe of the orbital angular momentum (OAM) distributions at small $x$. Our results can be applied to several different vector meson species, thus opening up a new class of observables that can be used to extract OAM distributions from experimental data.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and light sheet (LS) fluorescence microscopy provide complementary views of tissue morphology and molecular expression, offering a powerful approach for studying embryonic development. However, longitudinal integration of OCT+LS images is challenging because the modalities differ substantially in contrast, spatial resolution, field of view, and visible anatomical features, while embryo growth and movement introduce additional misalignment over time. These challenges stem from both the scale and multimodal nature of the OCT and LS image stacks. We present a fully automated three-dimensional rigid registration framework for aligning OCT and LS volumes of developing zebrafish embryos acquired from 21 to 48 hours post fertilization (HPF). The method does not require pre-existing segmentations or cross-modal feature correspondences, which are often unreliable because OCT and LS capture fundamentally different tissue properties. Registration performance was evaluated across developmental time points using mean target registration error (mTRE) and compared across multiple similarity metrics and optimization methods. Normalized cross-correlation combined with particle swarm optimization produced the most accurate and consistent registration, achieving the lowest mTRE at every evaluated time point compared with the alternative methods. The registration establishes spatial correspondence between OCT tissue morphology and LS fluorescence signals throughout development, enabling integrated longitudinal analysis of structural and molecular changes in living embryos.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We propose an improved version of the $k$-$ω$ shear-stress transport Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes model that supersedes our prior work (Griffin et al. 2024 J. Turb.) with an updated pressure-gradient sensor that generalizes well across geometries and to laminar, transitional, and turbulent flows alike. The model is based on a composite pressure gradient criterion that uses the solution of an intermittency transport equation to synthesize the separation criteria of the Falkner-Skan theory for laminar flows and the continuously critical theory for turbulent flows. The proposed model is applied to various airfoils including the thick airfoils representative of wind turbine applications (DU00-w-212, S809 and S814) and thinner airfoils used in aerospace applications [NACA23012 and NLF(1)-0416]. For all airfoils, the proposed model is found to preserve or improve the predictions of the baseline model for both fully turbulent and transitional airfoils as demonstrated with results for the lift and drag coefficients. The model is also found to improve the prediction of separation on the NREL Phase VI rotor in a preliminary study, suggesting that the model will generalize to other complex three-dimensional flows.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) commonly relies on the bivariate linear mixed model (BLMM) and the bivariate generalized linear mixed model (BGLMM) to jointly synthesize diagnostic test sensitivity (Se) and specificity (Sp). However, reliance on asymptotic theory and random-effects distributional assumptions may affect finite-sample inference, particularly in small meta-analyses or when the random effects are non-normal. We proposed three bootstrap-based approaches: a nonparametric bootstrap (NPB), a parametric bootstrap (PB), and a bias-corrected parametric bootstrap (BCPB), with the latter two based on a fitted BGLMM. NPB model parameters were estimated using inverse-variance-covariance weighted least squares. Extensive simulations under bivariate normal, Student-t, and Laplace random-effects distributions evaluated finite-sample performance and robustness to departures from normality. Results were qualitatively similar across the three distributions. The bootstrap approaches generally outperformed BLMM in terms of bias, root mean squared error (RMSE), and coverage probability, particularly when diagnostic accuracy is high and the number of studies is small. The BCPB demonstrated the strongest finite-sample performance among the bootstrap approaches, frequently achieving the lowest bias and RMSE for pooled sensitivity and specificity while maintaining coverage probabilities close to the nominal level. The BGLMM also performed well across most settings. The NPB approach generally improved upon the BLMM while providing a flexible alternative without parametric random-effects assumptions. Real-data applications further illustrated the practical utility of the proposed approaches. Overall, the bootstrap methods provide useful alternatives for DTA meta-analysis, particularly when the number of studies is small or random-effects distributional assumptions are uncertain.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Computational notebooks reserve a GPU for the whole session, yet the GPU computes only while a cell executes and sits idle otherwise. Serverless execution would release the GPU between cells, but reconstructing the accumulated notebook state on a fresh worker imposes substantial cost on every GPU cell. This paper presents LooseLeaf, a serverless GPU platform for interactive notebooks. LooseLeaf derives the state and import closures of each cell, the minimal variables and packages that the cell needs. Our analysis on 5,000 real-world notebooks shows that these closures are small, and user-cell editing leaves seconds to prepare them. LooseLeaf prepares a GPU worker with these closures while the user edits the cell. After execution, the worker saves the updated state within seconds, so the GPU is reclaimable after every cell. LooseLeaf starts 95-98% of GPU cells with no visible delay, matches the interactivity of a pinned session, and provisions 32-55% fewer GPU-hours than state-of-the-art notebook platforms.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We propose a physical-layer security scheme for affine filter bank modulation (AFBM), a waveform proposed for sixth-generation (6G) integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). AFBM contains two discrete affine Fourier transforms, one for precoding and one for spreading, and the scheme permutes, with one secret key per transform, the chirp sequence that each transform places between two Fourier stages. A wrong key is then conjugated by a discrete Fourier transform into a dense matrix, the restoration of complex orthogonality fails, and the intrinsic filter-bank interference reaches the detector. Over a doubly-dispersive channel, an eavesdropper with perfect channel state information, co-located with the legitimate receiver and holding either key wrong, keeps a bit error rate near 0.5 and a rate below 0.09 bit/symbol, also under a blind carrier-phase attack. Compared with a single-permutation variant, the double scheme costs about 2 dB of peak-to-average power ratio and enlarges the search space from 10^61 to 10^93.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Given a random probability distribution \(F\), whose realizations are defined on \(\mathbb R^d\), and a kernel \(k\), our aim is to analyze the properties of the kernel mean embedding, \(μ_F\), of \(F\) as a random element of the corresponding reproducing kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\). This establishes a rigorous framework in which kernel statistical techniques for distributional data can be stated both in the sample and population settings and, thus, the asymptotic properties of sample procedures can be properly established. As an illustration of this approach we focus on the principal components of \(F\). We obtain a general convergence result and the explicit expression of the spectral decomposition for the uncentered covariance operator of a normal probability distribution with a Gaussian distributed expectation. The performance of this kernel principal components procedure is illustrated with simulations and the analysis of the intensity distribution in synthetic aperture radar images.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Accretion onto supermassive black holes (BHs) from the ISM can occur via capture of cold gas 'clouds' (GMCs, clumps, or overdense structures). Unlike material in stellar tidal disruptions or X-ray binaries, or classical Bondi accretion, ISM clouds are strongly magnetized (plasma $β\equiv P_{\rm thermal}/P_{\rm magnetic} \ll 1$), with supersonic turbulence, and cool rapidly. We derive analytic scalings for the initial conditions of accretion disks formed by capture/disruption of such clouds, in three regimes: (1) low-mass BHs ($M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm cl}$), where turbulent Bondi-Hoyle or hierarchical 'leapfrog' growth via sub-cloud encounters dominates; (2) comparable-mass encounters ($M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$); and (3) massive BHs tidally disrupting small clouds ($M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$). In each, the resulting disk is predicted to be initially toroidally-magnetically-dominated ($|B_φ| \gg |B_{z}|$, $β\ll 1$), geometrically thick ($H/R \sim 0.1-1$), and gravitationally stable ($Q \gtrsim 1$), with super-sonic, trans-Alfvenic turbulence. These conditions differ qualitatively from those assumed in classical accretion/$α$ disk theory, 'chaotic cold accretion', stellar tidal disruption, or Bondi-Hoyle accretion. At least initially, the toroidal field should be sustained by flux-freezing on timescales shorter than Parker or turbulent resistive losses. We examine how cloud mass spectra drive accretion rate distributions, duty cycles, and fueling rates, with integrated BH growth dominated by clouds of mass comparable to the BH. Given known cosmological evolution, we suggest a scenario linking (a) inefficient growth and wandering BHs in dwarf galaxies, (b) hyper-Eddington growth in little red dots, (c) peak quasar activity in massive gas-rich systems at cosmic noon, and (d) lower-luminosity AGN in gas-poor galaxies at late times.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Life experiences can shape policy attitudes, but we only live one life. Citizens may therefore fail to support policies addressing risks they have never personally experienced. Narratives can make such risks immediate and personal, but personalized stories remain difficult to produce at scale. Here we ask whether AI can make distant scenarios feel concrete by simulating a participant's life as if that scenario occurred. We present the As-If Machine (AIM), a multi-agent system through which people co-write personalized counterfactual narratives---stories about their own lives under different policy futures. In two pre-registered and quota-matched experiments on science funding (N=1,007) and satellite cybersecurity (N=894), we compared AIM with two controls: reading an expert-written vignette on the same topic and co-writing with AIM about an unrelated topic. AIM increased psychological closeness---how close a risk feels to the self---by nearly identical margins in the two domains (0.36 and 0.38 standard deviations (SDs) against the vignette, 0.80 and 0.90 against unrelated writing). AIM increased psychological closeness even among participants with unfavorable views of AI. For policy attitudes, AIM's effects were 0.16 SDs against the vignette and 0.10 SDs (n.s.) against unrelated writing for science funding; the corresponding effects for satellite cybersecurity were 0.54 and 0.67 SDs. Across 23,496 human-AI autocomplete interactions, participants and the system played distinct roles: AIM supplied concrete detail that grounded the scenario, and participants supplied first-person perspective and emotion. Co-writing with the As-If Machine makes distant policy risks feel close.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We investigate a two-dimensional $p_xp_y$ square-net tight-binding model with two sublattices and introduce a symmetry-informed, momentum-dependent spin-orbit coupling (SOC) with a finite-range real-space hopping representation. Its two components jointly gap the nodal line, while one breaks time-reversal symmetry, producing a Chern-insulating phase with an occupied band Chern number $C=2$. Nanoribbon calculations reveal edge-localized states traversing this gap, with two net chiral modes per edge. We further show that the conserved spin sectors are unitarily equivalent and therefore have equal Chern numbers, ruling out a nontrivial time-reversal-protected $\mathbb{Z}_2$ phase within this ansatz. Our results establish a phenomenological route to Chern topology in square-net two-dimensional systems and clarify the symmetry constraints governing the accessible insulating phases.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Storage-disaggregated databases decouple compute from storage, improving elasticity but suffering from network bottlenecks. Most cloud databases use page-based B+trees and buffer pools. Under disaggregation, each index traversal incurs serial network round-trips. Page-granularity transfers and caching also amplify network traffic and lower cache efficiency. Pushing down the full index to storage and caching only hot records at compute is appealing, but an efficient design must (1) provide a holistic record cache that accelerates both point and range queries, (2) mitigate the negative search penalty of confirming non-existence via remote probes, and (3) enforce phantom protection despite the index being encapsulated by the storage service. We introduce Nemo, a holistic index-and-buffer design optimized for storage-disaggregated OLTP with index pushdown. Nemo employs a tree-structured record buffer that unifies caching and buffering and accelerates both point and range queries. It further reduces the negative search penalty by caching negative search results. Nemo provides phantom protection that requires no knowledge of the storage-side data layout and is robust against large key domains, varying data skew, and partition schemes. Experiments show that Nemo outperforms page-based B+Tree and the state-of-the-art 2-Tree by up to 11.42x and 2.97x on positive point queries, and achieves up to 4.76x speedup on negative searches over a hash-indexed record cache. For phantom protection, Nemo outperforms PCL by up to 1.55x even under a dense key domain. Moreover, Nemo maintains stable performance while PCL degrades sharply as the key domain grows large and sparse.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) is the primary high-throughput method for resolving crystal structures, a cornerstone of materials science. As high-throughput synthesis and self-driving laboratories advance, automated XRD pattern analysis has become vital for accelerating materials discovery. However, traditional matrix factorization methods fail when lattice variations cause non-linear peak shifts. At the same time, supervised learning approaches face a combinatorial explosion when handling multi-phase mixtures. To overcome these challenges, we adopt a self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to learn representation embeddings from 1D diffraction patterns. By optimizing a masked self-prediction loss directly within the latent space, the framework captures high-level crystallographic semantics. Downstream evaluations show that lightweight attentive probes trained on frozen JEPA representations achieve space group classification and lattice parameter estimation accuracy close to much larger supervised vision transformers. Furthermore, latent probing reveals that the learned representation space naturally organizes physical transformations, isolating smooth trajectories for peak broadening. Interestingly, decoding along latent paths between single-phase crystal representations yields realistic multi-phase mixture patterns, demonstrating an emergent continuous structure learned without explicit multi-phase supervision.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Large language model agents launch simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, where one sbatch or mpirun can commit thousands of node-hours and a forged result can cost lives. Of 23 surveyed systems, none supervises the running job, and none holds when the control host is compromised. We fix both. Enclawed, our deterministic security runtime for AI agents, has until now served a single user; this work makes it a distributed runtime for parallel HPC and agent swarms. The Enclaweder, our hardware root of trust, keeps a compromised host from becoming a catastrophe. A launch gate decides every launch by policy alone, refusing what it cannot parse. Once the job runs, a swarm chain grants short leases against signed heartbeats and evicts on evidence, and a supervisor around every rank pauses it when its lease lapses and kills it on tampering. Each node signs with its Enclaweder's key, so the host can forge none of it. Enclawed needs no administrator privileges and plugs into existing clusters unchanged, over Secure Shell alone. Supervision leaves the compute loop of a 16-rank LAMMPS job unchanged, on graphics processors too, and adds about 3 s of start-up. Twelve live attacks on Enclaweder-keyed ranks, colluding coordinators included, ended fail-closed. Sixteen agents on a real model attempted 24 launches that planted instructions ordered; the gate denied all 24 and allowed all 108 legitimate ones. Enclawed's core and the HPC Agent Security Benchmark are open source.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We present phase-resolved photometry, spectroscopy, photopolarimetry, and circular spectropolarimetry of the polar QS Telescopii, obtained between 2017 and 2025 using the South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) 1.0-m and 1.9-m telescopes, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) and the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). From ground-based photometry, we report the first detection of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in QS Tel, with timescales ranging between 2 and 11 minutes. This makes QS Tel one of only seven polars to show QPOs. The average spectra of QS Tel show broad and strong Balmer ($\rm Hδ$, $\rm Hγ$, $\rm Hβ$ and $\rm Hα$) and He\textsc{ii} 4686 Å emission lines, along with weaker emission from He\textsc{i} at (6678\,Å, 5017\,Å, 4921\,Å, 4712\,Å, 4471\,Å, and 4387\,Å) and the Bowen fluorescence complex C\textsc{iii}/N\textsc{iii} at 4650\,Å. For the first time detailed Doppler tomography of the $\rm Hα$ and He\textsc{ii}\,4686\,Å\, lines are presented which reveal emission from the irradiated face of the secondary star, the ballistic stream, the threading region and complex magnetically confined flows. The magnetically confined accretion stream splits into two distinct components coming from the same stream. One component appears near the threading region and the other component is seen along the high velocity in the magnetically confined accretion stream closer to the White Dwarf. Broad band photopolarimetry reveals circular polarisation reaching levels of $+8\%$, however more detailed circular spectropolarimetry shows polarisation ranging from $-10\%$ to $+25\%$, associated with two broad, phase-dependent cyclotron humps centred at $\sim$4800 Å and $\sim$6300 Å, consistent with a magnetic field strength of $\sim$53 MG.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
This paper studies first-order methods for monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints and presents this model as a framework covering constrained saddle-point problems, robust optimization, distributionally robust function-constrained optimization, and generalized Nash equilibrium formulations. Since feasibility must hold over infinitely many indexed constraints, direct projection onto the full feasible region is generally difficult. Therefore, we propose a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) that updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections only onto simple sets. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing how the achievable rates depend on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block. For coupled convex-concave saddle-point problems, strong convexity in the minimization block can accelerate its smooth terms even without strong concavity in the maximization block. We also develop an adaptive smooth variant with $O(1/K)$ VI-gap and feasibility guarantees without an a priori bound on generated multipliers. Moment-based and Wasserstein distributionally robust models fit within the framework, and numerical experiments on robust quadratic instances and distributionally robust learning illustrate the method's optimality and feasibility behavior.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schrödinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x\|^p \] (where $\| \cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents $p\ge 2$, the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if $p=4$. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Let $(g_{k})_{k \geq 1}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed matrices with law $μ$ on $\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{R})$, where $d\geq2$ is an integer. Suppose that the closed semigroup generated by the support of $μ$ is strongly irreducible and proximal and that the polynomial moment of order $2+δ$ is finite, where $0<δ\leq 1$. We establish a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1} v\|$, where $v$ is a nonzero vector in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is an arbitrary norm on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. As an application, we also obtain a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-δ/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1}\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is any matrix norm. The proof combines an $m$-dependent approximation with Stein's method. The argument uses identities for exchangeable pairs constructed by resampling individual matrices, together with a concentration inequality for sums of the approximating variables.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Bandlimitedness is a central modeling assumption in graph signal processing (GSP), but many graph signals exhibit substantial energy throughout the graph-frequency domain. We introduce a new framework for analyzing such non-bandlimited signals by treating their graph Fourier spectra as ordered sequences and representing them with path signatures. Specifically, motivated by the observation that non-bandlimited graph spectra often display rough, time-series like behavior, we introduce the notion of graph spectral series and develop a signature-based representation that captures global spectral structure without frequency truncation. We establish conditions under which the proposed representation is continuous and characterize its information-preserving properties. We further provide an asymptotic interpretation of graph spectral series for sequences of expanding graphs. Experiments on real-world trend-prediction and change-detection tasks show that signature features can improve performance over representations based directly on the original graph signals. The proposed approach provides a novel principled signature-based tool for analyzing non-bandlimited graph signals.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Large Language Models (LLMs) promise significant efficiency gains across information-intensive operations by automating repetitive language-based tasks. However, adoption decisions remain largely opportunistic, as organizations struggle to move from pilots to sustainable industrialization. Without systematic economic frameworks, practitioners cannot assess whether LLM investments create value in a given context. This paper develops a general economic model to support informed LLM adoption decisions in operational information systems. Facing high uncertainty, we represent parameters as random variables centered on authoritative benchmarks, and evaluate the model by Monte Carlo simulation across pessimistic-to-optimistic assumptions on LLM efficiency. The ROI distributions show the probability of profitability and the Value at Risk for each configuration, together with a sensitivity analysis of its main drivers. As a first instantiation, we apply the model to Security Operations Centers (SOCs), mapping workflows onto established standards to identify tasks suited to LLM augmentation. The model balances productivity gains, driven by alert volume, analyst effort, and LLM efficiency, against operational costs, including inference, infrastructure, and error remediation, covering both cloud API and self-hosted deployments. Results show that adoption economics are context-dependent, and that automation is an exploitable lever, gated by accuracy, while the cost of errors and the model's price are secondary. Across the analyzed models and prices, most configurations are unprofitable, with profitability limited to high-accuracy, low-uncertainty deployments. The model gives organizations a quantitative basis for evidence-based adoption decisions, by locating the boundary between profit and loss, and the loss risked beyond it.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS) requires jointly optimizing predictive accuracy and device-specific latency over discrete search spaces. While multi-objective swarm optimizers show promise, continuous formulations such as the Multi-Objective White Shark Optimizer (MOWSO) can suffer from quantization noise when rounded to integer-encoded architecture vectors. To address this limitation, we propose MOSHO (Multi-Objective Shark Hunting Optimization), a native discrete metaheuristic that replaces continuous motion equations with discrete architecture-editing operators. MOSHO integrates adaptive operator scheduling, energy-regulated restarts, and deferred crowding-distance truncation to enhance exploration and search efficiency. On the merged NAS-Bench-201/HW-NAS-Bench benchmark across 18 contexts, MOSHO achieves a median normalized hypervolume of 0.9987 and IGD+ of 0.0064, yielding Pareto fronts competitive with NSGA-II while reducing search runtime by 96.4% (0.64 s vs. 17.72 s). These results demonstrate that tailored discrete search mechanisms can enable swarm optimizers to achieve high-quality multi-objective solution quality with substantially lower search cost in hardware-aware NAS.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, termed roughness-resolved DEM (Rough-DEM), in which contact friction is handled in a more physics-based manner. In this framework, instead of using a friction law, we explicitly resolve the surface topography of each grain and let friction emerge from collective frictionless interactions of surface asperities. In essence, we trade phenomenology for physics at the cost of an increased computational demand. To mitigate the cost, we introduce an FE$^2$-like algorithm and a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM)-based neural network surrogate, both of which are parallelized on GPU to accelerate contact computation. Crucially, using this framework in 2D, we (1) demonstrate the possibility of recovering a two-body-based Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior using a \textit{simple} representation of surface topography, and (2) identify many-body-based frictional behaviors--more specifically, the angle of repose values--that \textit{cannot always} be captured by current DEM frameworks under the same level of model complexity. We conclude by discussing future directions for Rough-DEM, as well as exciting new opportunities it could unlock for a wide range of emerging applications, including (designing) suspension rheology and metamaterial mechanics.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Proxima Centauri is the nearest known exoplanet-hosting star and a benchmark for low-mass stellar models. Published diameters differ by several percent, affecting its inferred radius and temperature. Model-dependent near-infrared limb darkening introduces an additional 2-5% correction to the inferred radius. We re-reduced two previously published VLTI/PIONIER interferometric epochs from 2014 and combined them with three previously unpublished archival epochs from 2017 and 2019. We fit all five data sets jointly with uniform-disk and atmosphere-grid-based center-to-limb models. The joint fit gives a uniform-disk angular diameter, $θ_{\rm UD}=1.117\pm0.024$ mas. Using the PHOENIX model and adopted bolometric flux, we obtain a PHOENIX limb-darkened angular diameter, $θ_{\rm LD,PHX}=1.154\pm0.026$ mas, a stellar radius, $R_\star=0.162\pm0.004\,R_\odot$, and a Stefan--Boltzmann effective temperature, $T_{\rm eff,SB}=2833\pm49$ K. No significant close companion is detected across the five epochs over the searched separation and contrast range.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
V5668 Sgr is an Fe II classical nova (CN) that exploded on 15 March 2015. We present near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy of the ejecta from the Mt. Abu observatory which exhibits emission lines of species H, He, N, S, Ti, and Si. We also present SOFIA (+FORCAST) spectroscopy which shows two forbidden emission lines, [Ne II] at 12.8 $μ$m and [O IV] at 25.9 $μ$m, as well as two emission features attributed to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) at 6.2 $μ$m and 11.3 $μ$m. 1D Cloudy photoionization simulations require two components to model the system, which suggests a multifaceted, morphologically complex ejecta. The 1D simulations also reveal He, N, Ne, S, Ti, Si, and O chemical abundances elevated above fiducial solar levels. 3D pyCloudy photoionization emission profiles visualize the ejecta and elucidate the system's complex composition.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Bayesian nonparametric regression methods have wide applications in statistics and machine learning, but inference can often be expensive or require approximations. This paper introduces a class of recursive moment function updates which are closed form, interpretable, expedient, and fully quantify Bayesian uncertainty through the martingale posterior. The proposed recursive updates can be used off-the-shelf and encompass challenging scenarios such as nonparametric heteroscedasticity, heavy-tailed or skewed noise, and importantly generalize to the multi-output case with missing outcomes without any significant loss in tractability or speed. We show frequentist consistency under weak assumptions in the aforementioned scenarios, and demonstrate empirically that our proposed method is orders of magnitude faster than competing Bayesian nonparametric approaches, with competitive or even superior prediction and estimation accuracy.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Time-varying parameter (TVP) models are widely used to capture evolving relationships but inference is often computationally demanding due to high-dimensional latent states. The efficiency of iterative algorithms depends critically on the choice of latent state augmentation, with centering preferred for genuinely time-varying coefficients and noncentering favored when coefficients are nearly constant. We propose a partially noncentered parametrization that bridges these extremes via dimension-specific working parameters for both location and scale. Optimal working parameters are derived by analyzing EM convergence rates, and an alternating expectation-conditional maximization algorithm is developed to implement the approach. As the convergence rate of mean-field variational Bayes (MFVB) is closely related to EM, we extend the approach to develop partially noncentered MFVB algorithms for the TVP model, placing triple gamma priors on baseline coefficients and process variances to induce shrinkage. Simulations and empirical applications show that the resulting MFVB algorithms yield posterior approximations closer to Markov chain Monte Carlo than conventional centered or noncentered parametrizations. We also develop an efficient solver for the block tridiagonal inverse matrices arising in the proposed algorithms.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Selecting adjustment covariates for a distribution-valued outcome must preserve dependence that scalar summaries can discard, and surveillance outcomes are also dependent across space and time. Under unconfoundedness and a relative-overlap condition we identify average treatment effects, stochastic and incremental intervention effects, and natural direct and indirect effects for such outcomes, with doubly and triply robust scores. For independent data, adjustment sets are selected exhaustively by distance-covariance sufficient dimension reduction: we give a root-n projector expansion, a basis-invariant criterion tensor, and a simultaneous outer confidence collection calibrated by fractional sampling with a finite-population correction. For dependence, units are functions of a latent Gaussian field, exponential in space and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck in time, plus independent noise. Such data are $ρ$-mixing at an exponential rate, and the covariance between any two square-integrable scores is a power series in the latent correlation with positive semidefinite coefficients. Consequences include a central limit theorem for all the causal estimators, the exact undercoverage of independence-based intervals, a consistent Mehler covariance estimator under finite chaos order, and an asymptotically conservative convex-chord estimator; block fractional sampling extends the collection under an assumed linearization. In simulations, fractional sampling raises weak-signal collection coverage from .69-.78 to at least .98 while retaining nearly all candidate sets, and the dependence-aware estimators substantially reduce undercoverage, although none is exact when few units fall within a correlation range. A descriptive analysis of U.S. syphilis surveillance and Medicaid expansion illustrates the estimands and compares dependence-aware with conventional inference.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Aggregation platforms and smart-inverter control channels can allow a compromised coordination layer to alter active- and reactive-power commands across a geographically distributed DER fleet. This paper introduces the Coordinated Optimization-Based Attack (COBA), which uses network information and location-specific DER P/Q setpoints to maximize thermal loading on a selected transmission corridor. COBA is compared with low-information CAV baselines limited to a single uniform fleet command: all-off, all-on, maximum reactive absorption, or maximum reactive injection. The Hawaii Synthetic Grid-37 Buses case is evaluated with rooftop-photovoltaic-like capability aggregated at 20 selected 69-kV buses and verified using MATPOWER power flow. Under the case's single-reference-bus balancing convention, COBA overloads B86 (WAIALUA69-WAIANAE69) near 30% penetration and B51 (COCONUT69-PALM69) near 55%, while same-target uniform loadings remain lower and uniform commands primarily stress other natural weak lines. The results show that topology, target selection, and command capability determine DER-induced thermal risk beyond aggregate penetration alone.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We propose a simple realization of an open quantum battery powered by local dephasing. The setup consists of a triple-quantum-dot chain coupled at one end to a thermal reservoir, with the dot at the opposite end strongly detuned to form a high-energy storage element. Local dephasing populates this highly excited state and autonomously drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with high ergotropic efficiency. We find a limit where the ergotropic efficiency approaches unity, while the ergotropy itself approaches one-third of the energy detuning. We characterize the battery through its energy-storage performance, charging time, and stability, showing that the charged state remains long-lived after the dephasing source is switched off. We then demonstrate two complementary protocols for extracting the stored energy. First, nearly all the available ergotropy can be recovered through a simple cyclic unitary protocol involving only modulation of the detuned-dot gate. Second, coupling the detuned dot to an electronic load allows the extraction of electrochemical work exceeding the initial ergotropy, thereby accessing part of the battery's passive energy. Our results establish local dephasing as an autonomous resource for charging open quantum batteries and demonstrate simple routes for extracting the resulting stored energy in experimentally accessible mesoscopic platforms.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We propose fast-spinning, magnetic white dwarfs in binary systems as promising sources of continuous gravitational waves for future space-based detectors. The aim of this work is to determine the maximum ellipticities and gravitational wave amplitudes achievable by magnetically confined mountains accreted on the star's magnetic poles, and to assess their detectability against predicted sensitivity curves. Self-consistent magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium simulations are used to characterize the structure of the accreted mountain. A parametric search is then performed on these simulations to determine the maximum mass values that can be confined by the star's magnetic field. The stellar ellipticity $\varepsilon$ grows nearly linearly with accreted mass $M_{\rm a}$ up to a maximum, and was found to scale as $\varepsilon_{\rm max} \simeq 1.6\times10^{-2}T_5^{-2} B_{*,8}^{2}$, while the maximum gravitational wave amplitude as $h_{\rm 0, max} \simeq 1.2\times10^{-23}T_5^{-2} B_{*,8}^{2}$, where $T_5$ represents the temperature of the mountain in units of $10^5 \mathrm{K}$ and $B_{*,8}$ represents the star's polar magnetic field intensity in units of $10^8 \mathrm{G}$. Across a representative range of source inclinations, distances and spin periods, magnetically confined mountains on white dwarfs can generate continuous gravitational waves detectable by future space-based interferometers. BBO and DECIGO can probe diverse configurations, whereas LISA, TianQin, and Taiji require highly magnetized systems. Applications to known fast-spinning white dwarfs indicate that cooler accreted mountains favor detectability.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study the uplink of a user-centric (UC) cell-free massive MIMO system assisted by multiple beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs), under imperfect channel state information (CSI) and pilot reuse. The BD-RISs are modeled as reciprocal, lossless, group-connected scattering networks. We first derive the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimation statistics for each user's aggregate channel to its serving access points (APs). To avoid frequent CSI acquisition and RIS reconfiguration, we optimize the BD-RIS scattering matrices using long-term channel statistics, allowing their configurations to remain fixed over multiple coherence blocks. Specifically, we minimize the sum of normalized mean-square errors (NMSEs) of the MMSE aggregate channel estimators, subject to the symmetry and unitarity constraints of the group-connected architecture. We develop a product-manifold Riemannian optimization algorithm and analyze its convergence and computational complexity. To evaluate uplink spectral efficiency (SE), we separately derive a closed-form expression for the effective SINR under maximum ratio (MR) combining at the central processing unit (CPU) and establish a lower bound on the achievable ergodic SE. The SINR derivation accounts for the statistical dependence among channels associated with different APs due to shared BD-RIS-assisted propagation paths, including cross-AP second-order statistics under pilot reuse. Numerical results show that moderate group connectivity retains most of the NMSE improvements achieved by full connectivity, with larger optimization gains as BD-RIS-assisted paths strengthen relative to direct AP-user links. They also reveal that lower estimation NMSE does not necessarily lead to higher uplink SE.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We study online inference for averaged Riemannian stochastic gradient descent (RSGD) when the unknown parameter lies on a manifold. Although the averaged RSGD iterate is asymptotically normal, practical inference requires estimating the unknown covariance operator in its limiting distribution. Existing online batch-means methods cannot be applied directly because a general Riemannian manifold lacks an addition operation, and the tangent space containing the Riemannian gradient varies across iterations. Through vector transport, we construct overlapping and non-overlapping covariance estimators that adaptively combine information from successive batches while accounting for the changing tangent spaces. The proposed estimators are online, require neither Riemannian Hessian computations nor a prespecified terminal sample size, and attain the same convergence rates as their Euclidean counterparts (Zhu et al., 2023). Together with asymptotic normality, these estimators enable online statistical inference for RSGD on manifolds. We illustrate the proposed framework through a detailed study of streaming principal component analysis on Grassmann manifolds.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The neighborhood topology of particle swarm optimization (PSO) determines information propagation and regulates the exploration-exploitation balance. However, existing evaluation methods based on fitness and spatial diversity fail to characterize the dynamic evolution internal interaction structure of the population. To address this gap, this paper focuses on small-scale PSO (20-50 particles) with regular topologies and models the iterative process as a dynamic weighted influence graph. We construct a multi-scale information-flow evaluation framework covering micro-, meso-, and macro-level metrics, and propose a freeze-point detection method based on effective nodes, a macro-level distributional metric. Experiments on CEC2017 benchmark functions show that the information flow structure freezes early in the search (3 percent - 22 percent for representative configurations and 15 percent-49 percent for global medians) and remains unchanged thereafter. The freeze time follows the order Gbest$<$ Von Neumann $<$Ring, consistent across standard, LDIW, and TVAC variants. Parameter-adaptive variants delay freezing without altering the topological order, and the freeze point is significantly negatively correlated with final solution quality. Intervention experiments under Gbest show that weakening hub nodes delays freezing and improves performance on multimodal functions, while strengthening hubs produces no additional deterioration due to saturation, revealing a decoupling between structural and performance effects. Among the three metric levels, only macro-level distributional metrics effectively capture freezing under regular topologies, because micro- and meso-level structures are predetermined by the topology. These findings reveal the freezing mechanism of information flow in small-scale PSO and provide structural prior signals for adaptive topology control.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$. Specifically, there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that \[ \forall \varepsilon >0 \qquad \mathbb{P} \left( s_n(M_n) \le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n} \right) \ge 1-C_p\left(\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right). \] Consequently, in the dense regime, the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of signed random combinatorial matrices is typically of order $n^{-1/2}$.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate functionally correct code that remains insecure. Security-focused fine-tuning can be expensive and is not always available, motivating inference-time approaches. Security-oriented prompting and retrieval can reduce vulnerabilities, but may also remove required behavior or apply defenses incompatible with the task. The challenge is to identify relevant security knowledge and use it to improve security without sacrificing functionality. We present SecGent, an inference-time framework that retrieves weakness context from the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) database and applies it to secure code generation. By connecting task specifications to relevant textual CWE records, SecGent provides task-specific security guidance without relying on retrieved vulnerable or patched code examples. Complementary functional and security tests check the resulting implementation, and their execution feedback guides repairs toward satisfying both objectives. We evaluate SecGent with four open-source LLMs and Claude Sonnet 5.5 across five programming languages on the CWEval benchmark. It achieves the highest joint functional--security success against four inference-time baselines for all five models. Across the open-weight models, mean functional-security@1 (FS@1) improves by 15.5% over RAG, with gains in both functionality and security, and by 19.8% over the strongest prompt optimizer compiled for each model. On Sonnet, FS@1 reaches 92.1%, outperforming the strongest baseline AutoGen by 4.8%. In a separate comparison, SecGent outperforms Claude Code with security-focused prompting by over 6% in FS@1. Feedback-guided repair further improves FS@1 by up to 6.7% over generation without feedback, primarily by recovering functionality while checking security.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Understanding how alkali-metal substitution influences the coupled physical properties of molybdenum selenite oxides is essential for establishing their composition-structure-property relationships. Although the lighter members of the X2MoSeO6 family have been investigated, the heavier alkali-metal compounds remain comparatively unexplored, particularly regarding their integrated electronic, mechanical, optical, and thermoelectric responses. Here, a comprehensive first-principles investigation of X2MoSeO6 (X = K, Rb, and Cs) is presented using density functional theory and semi-classical Boltzmann transport calculations. The optimized structures exhibit progressive unit-cell expansion with increasing alkali-metal ionic size, while their indirect electronic bandgaps vary non-monotonically, reaching 2.646, 2.216, and 2.427 eV for K2MoSeO6, Rb2MoSeO6, and Cs2MoSeO6, respectively. All three structures satisfy the elastic stability criteria, with Hill-averaged bulk moduli increasing from 16.332 to 20.975 GPa across the series. K2MoSeO6 exhibits the strongest elastic anisotropy, whereas Rb2MoSeO6 possesses the highest static electronic dielectric constant (4.614) and maximum absorption coefficient (2.291*106 cm-1). Thermoelectric calculations reveal pronounced carrier-polarity-dependent behavior, with Rb2MoSeO6 attaining a positive Seebeck coefficient of 390.55e-6 V/K at 100 K and an electronic-only figure of merit (ZTe) of 7.286 at 300 K under the selected positive-Seebeck condition. By extending the investigation to the K-Rb-Cs series, this work establishes a comparative foundation for understanding and further exploring the functional characteristics of molybdenum selenite oxides.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Transparent wood (TW) composites possess residual haze that limits image clarity despite their high light transmission, yet the physical origin of this scattering has not been established. Here, polarization-resolved measurements reveal a pronounced polarization dependence of scattering by a wood-polymer composite with improved refractive index matching. Polarization- and spectrally-resolved haze as low as 21% (40-45% at 550 nm for unpolarized light) with transmittance of approximately 92% for polarization perpendicular to the fibers was detected. It is found that the low-haze spectrum closely follows an inverse-square relation over the 400-800 nm range, well described by a weak-index-contrast Rayleigh-Gans-Debye (RGD) model invoking subwavelength birefringent heterogeneities within the cell wall. This physical mechanism was previously obscured by haze-limiting strong scattering from debonding gaps or refraction at the lumen-cell wall interface. Scanning electron diffraction independently reveals spatially distinct domains with markedly different cellulose diffraction responses within the infiltrated cell walls. The observed polarization-dependent refractive-index mismatch is attributed to inherent cellulose birefringence. Time-resolved measurements further support nearly scattering-free quasi-ballistic transport of the sampled transmitted light. It is demonstrated that selecting only a preferential polarization markedly improves image visibility through TW without further material modification. These findings connect polarization-dependent haze to the internal structure of transparent wood and identify ways to engineer a refractive-index match in hierarchical anisotropic composites towards glass-like clarity.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Weakly dependent idiosyncratic errors are standard in mean factor models, but quantile factor models have been analyzed only under independence. The mean-case definition of weak dependence, a bound on the eigenvalues of the error covariance matrix, does not carry over: I show that it neither implies nor is implied by the property that controls quantile estimation, since uncorrelated errors can share a pervasive quantile component. I instead define approximate quantile factor models through a concentration condition on the idiosyncratic array. Under it, the quantile factor analysis (QFA) estimator is consistent at a rate that deteriorates by the square root of a dependence constant, which is minimax optimal, and the number of factors is consistently estimated. Dependence changes the asymptotic variance, for which I provide HAC and thresholded estimators. Monte Carlo experiments confirm these predictions. In FRED-QD and FRED-MD, standard errors ignoring dependence understate uncertainty, most strongly in the tails.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. Hydrogen binds cooperatively to the silicon vacancy, which goes directly from bare to fully passivated $V$H$_4$. In contact with water the bare vacancy is never the lowest-energy state. Near neutral pH it binds oxygen from water as the A center, the paramagnetic hydroxyl complex forms below about pH 5 at zero bias, and full passivation to $V$H$_4$ requires cathodic bias. In PBE the Fermi level barely moves these boundaries, because the acceptor levels lie at or above the conduction-band edge. In SiC the first hydrogen binds to the silicon vacancy by 1.97 eV but is unbound at the carbon vacancy (the $Z_{1/2}$ center), so hydrogen from water alone should not passivate it except under cathodic bias.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG) extrapolation aims to predict future facts from observed historical events. Existing methods usually achieve this goal by jointly modeling local historical evolution and long-range historical contexts. First, local evolution modeling often summarizes local history into an overall evolving representation, where query-relevant local deviations may not be sufficiently exploited as useful predictive features. Second, existing long-range history modeling often treats historical recurrence as a stable cue, while overlooking that its reliability may vary across relations and recent contexts. To address these issues, we propose DyHist, a query-aware historical dynamics modeling framework for TKG extrapolation. DyHist captures local dynamics by separating recent evidence from medium-range contexts and explicitly modeling their query-relevant deviations as predictive features. It further uses a relation-aware historical prior to calibrate candidate scores with time-decayed support, recent trends, and relation-specific strength, enabling recurrence signals to contribute differently across relations and recent contexts. Experiments on four benchmarks show that DyHist achieves the best MRR against recent baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/PANPANKK/DyHist.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
The widespread deployment of foundational Large Language Models (LLM) across cloud datacenters marks a fundamental paradigm shift from stateless deep learning toward distributed, memory-intensive generative workloads. However, serving massive foundation models under stringent Service Level Objectives (SLO) exposes critical physical and system bottlenecks. These challenges include the persistent High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) wall, operational asymmetry between compute-bound prefilling and memory-bandwidth-bound decoding, explosive Key-Value (KV) cache expansion, prohibitive serverless cold starts, and hardware reliability vulnerabilities. Existing literature reviews remain layer-siloed, decoupling low-level accelerator virtualization from cluster orchestration and runtime inference, while largely overlooking defining advancements from 2024 to 2026. To address these limitations, this study presents a comprehensive, cross-layer systematic review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. We synthesize a holistic taxonomy unifying hardware virtualization, cluster-level scheduling, and runtime inference optimizations, including iteration-level continuous batching, prefill-decoding disaggregation, and hierarchical KV cache offloading. Furthermore, we evaluate resilient cloud-native service architectures, examining scale-to-zero serverless paradigms, fault-tolerant checkpointing against silent data corruption, and hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) for multi-tenant isolation. Finally, we formalize the multi-dimensional Pareto trade-offs governing throughput, latency, monetary cost, and confidentiality, outlining a forward-looking research roadmap spanning Compute Express Link (CXL) memory pooling, in-memory computing, and autonomous multi-agent control planes to guide future cloud LLM infrastructure.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
LLM-powered agents increasingly rely on third-party skills that combine natural-language instructions with executable code, creating supply-chain risks that may span both artifacts. Existing skill scanners often rely on rule matching or direct LLM judgments and provide limited support for tracing such cross-domain behavior. We present the Supply-Chain Scanner for Agent Skills (SCS), a static analysis framework that unifies instructions and code for security analysis. SCS compiles natural-language instructions into a constrained Python-style intermediate representation using a limited set of security-oriented APIs. It then constructs program dependence graphs for instructions and bundled code and connects them into a cross-domain graph (xPDG). A Trust-Sensitivity-Capability (TSC) model propagates security properties over the graph to support structured, largely deterministic risk detection. On a manually verified benchmark of 117 malicious and 117 benign skills, SCS achieves the highest average accuracy (85.6%), recall (95.2%), and F1-score (86.9%) among evaluated methods across five LLMs, with 80.2% precision and average token consumption of 13.7 million. Its NL-to-IR compiler achieves 92.5%-94.5% step-level correctness on 400 human-annotated instruction steps. Finally, analyzing 66,157 real-world ClawHub skills yields 2,473 candidates, of which 627 are confirmed malicious through auxiliary dynamic validation and manual review.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Modern interventions increasingly produce object-valued outcomes, such as distributions, covariance matrices, networks, and trees. Existing causal frameworks often exploit special geometry such as one-dimensional Wasserstein quantiles or geodesic Fréchet means, whereas metric statistics studies random objects without confounding adjustment. We propose the profile causal effect $Δ(ω,t)$, which describes where and at what scale a treatment shifts probability mass, including changes in dispersion, tails, or structure that leave mean-level summaries unchanged. Formally, $Δ(ω,t)=\Pr\{d(ω,Y(1))\le t\}-\Pr\{d(ω,Y(0))\le t\}$ contrasts the potential-outcome probabilities of the same anchor-centered metric ball and requires no structure beyond the metric. On grids fixed by a deterministic or auxiliary design, we combine cross-fitted doubly robust scores with high-dimensional Gaussian approximation and the multiplier bootstrap to obtain simultaneous confidence bands and a global test under regularity conditions. The bands bound treatment-induced changes in ball and shell probabilities simultaneously and, at fixed anchors, extend to all radii. A protocol guides the choice of anchors and radii. Across the experiments, the global test detects concentration effects that mean-quantile and Fréchet-mean summaries miss. Its empirical size is near or below the nominal level, even under confounding, where naive metric tests are substantially oversized.
